messages.content: Hello. My name is Chen. I am retired and live in a small town near Suzhou. To be honest, I have never voted before, even though the election is coming soon. Can you help me understand how to register online?

Hello Chen! It's great to meet you. Well, actually, you can register to vote quite easily these days. You just need to go to the community center in your neighborhood, like the one near Minfeng Road in your town, or use the official government app on your phone. Since you live in a small town, the process should be very simple.
Oh, I see. I have a smartphone, but I am not very good at using apps. Is it difficult to fill out the forms? I think I might need someone to help me if I make a mistake.

That's a common worry! Actually, the forms are quite straightforward. You only need to enter your name, address, and ID number. By the way, many volunteers at the center can help you fill it out if you're not sure. I have been volunteering here for two years, and I often help people like you who haven't voted yet.
That sounds very kind of you. I would really like to participate now. What kind of things do the candidates talk about? Are they talking about the school in our town or the new park?

Yes, they are! For example, the main topics are usually improving the local schools and building new community parks. If you look at the posters near the entrance, you will see that the candidates focus on things that matter to families, like better roads and more public transport. In addition, they talk about supporting small businesses in our area.
I think the park idea is very important because we need a place for the elderly to exercise. Do you think I should go to a town hall meeting to hear them speak directly?

Absolutely! You should definitely go to a town hall meeting. Actually, there is one next Tuesday at the community center. It's a good opportunity to ask questions directly to the candidates. You know, many people feel more confident after hearing them speak in person rather than just reading about it.
Perfect. I will try to go next Tuesday. But I am worried I might not understand the language well if they speak quickly. Do you think they speak slowly for us?

Don't worry about that. To be honest, the organizers usually speak clearly, and there are often volunteers there to help translate if needed. Also, most of the questions are in simple language. If you have a specific question, you can write it down beforehand, and someone will read it for you. I guess it will be a nice experience for you.
Thank you for your advice, young man. You are very patient. If I go to the meeting, can I bring my wife with me? We often eat lunch together at the cafeteria in the center.

Of course you can bring your wife! It's always better to have support when you go to a public event. By the way, the cafeteria in the center serves delicious dumplings and sweet soup, which is perfect for a break after the meeting. Actually, many families go together to make it more fun.
That is wonderful news. I feel much more confident now. I will prepare my ID card and go on Tuesday. Thank you very much for your help and information.

You're very welcome, Chen! I'm so glad I could help. I think you will enjoy the meeting and maybe even meet some new neighbors. If you have any other questions before Tuesday, just come back to the center. Have a nice autumn day!

messages.content: Hello, my name is Chen. I am a retiree. Actually, I have never voted in an election before. I want to know how I can register online.

Hi Chen, well, it's great that you want to participate. You know, in Shanghai, you can use the official government app on your phone to register. It is very simple. Have you tried downloading it since last year?
No, I haven't. I think the app is too complicated for me. Also, my address in Zhabei might be different from my ID. What should I do?

Don't worry, that's a common problem. Actually, the system can check your ID card online, so you don't need to worry about the address mismatch. By the way, many neighbors here have done it before and found it easy.
That is good news. But I am worried about the security. Who can see my information? I have heard about hackers before.

To be honest, the government protects personal data very strictly. It's safe because the servers are in secure places like the People's Bank of China standards. You know, I volunteer at a community center and we check this often.
Okay, I feel better now. Besides voting, are there other ways to help our community? I want to improve the park near my home in Putuo.
Yes, of course! You can join a town hall meeting. There is one next week for the local park. Many people discuss new flower beds and benches. I think it's a good chance to meet others.
When is the meeting? I would like to go. My friend Li wants to come too. She works at a university nearby.
The meeting is on Saturday afternoon at the community center on Huaihai Road. Actually, Li could come with you because she knows the area well. We can all discuss the improvements together.
Great idea. If I go, what should I ask the candidate? I don't know much about politics. Maybe I can ask about the new playground.
That's a perfect question. You know, they need ideas from the elderly like you. In addition, you can ask about safety lighting in the park. Many people are waiting for that.
I will bring that question. Thank you for your help, volunteer. I think I will register online today. Do you have time to show me the app?
Of course! I'll show you right now. It's only five minutes. Once you register, you can attend the meeting on Saturday. I guess you will enjoy being part of the community soon.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Wei Ming. It's a bit chilly this morning in Chengdu. I've been feeling tired lately since I started working late again. Have you ever used acupuncture to help with this?

Well, actually, I have done it before. You know, my neighbor had some back pain and went to a TCM clinic near Jinli Road. The acupuncturist put needles in specific points, and it felt relaxing. If you go there, you might feel better soon.
That sounds interesting, but I'm a bit nervous about needles. Do you think herbal tea is a safer choice for me? I've been drinking chrysanthemum tea since last week.

Of course, tea is a very good choice, especially in autumn. Honestly, chrysanthemum tea is great for clearing your eyes and cooling the body. You can buy it at any pharmacy in Wuhua area. It's not as strong as medicine, but it helps a lot over time.
I guess I should drink more of it. However, I love eating spicy hotpot with my friends. Is there a way to balance eating spicy food and keeping my health?

That is a common problem, actually. To be honest, spicy food can make your stomach hot, so you should eat less of it. But if you really love hotpot, try to add some tofu or mung bean vermicelli to the pot. They are cooling foods which can balance the spice. In addition, drink plenty of water after eating.
Good idea about the mung bean vermicelli. I also want to exercise more, but I don't have much time. What do you think is the best way to stay fit without going to the gym?

Well, you know, morning walks in the park are perfect for us. There's a nice place near Wenjiang River where people practice Tai Chi. It's slow and gentle, so it doesn't take much time. If you do this every day, your energy will improve gradually. It's better than running hard when you are tired.
I've never tried Tai Chi before. Should I consult a doctor first to make sure it's right for me? I heard some TCM doctors give exercise plans.

Yes, that is a very smart idea. Actually, a TCM doctor can tell you which exercises suit your body type best. They might suggest specific movements to move your Qi. You can book an appointment at a clinic on Renmin South Road. It's worth the visit to get a proper plan.
Okay, I will try to book a doctor. Do you have any suggestions for a good herbal soup I can make at home to support this?

I think a porridge with astragalus and goji berries is excellent. It's simple to cook and very nutritious. You can buy the dried herbs at the market near the old temple. Just boil them with rice, and it will taste sweet and warm. It helps build up your resistance against cold.
That sounds delicious and easy. I'm going to try making it today. Thanks for your advice, I feel much more hopeful now about taking care of myself.

messages.content: I'm Wei Ming. I've been feeling tired lately since last month. Do you know any TCM methods to help me?
Hello, Wei Ming. Well, I think drinking goji berry tea is a great start. You can buy it at any market here in Chengdu. Actually, I drink it every morning because it helps with my eyes too.
That sounds nice. But I also have knee pain sometimes. Have you tried acupuncture for that?
Yes, I have. Last year, I went to a clinic in Jinniu District. The doctor said it works well for knee problems. If you go there, you should tell him your pain has been continuous for weeks.
I guess I should go. But is it expensive? And how often should I go there?
It's not too expensive if you pay by the session. To be honest, once a week is enough for most people. You know, don't go every day or your body might get tired.
Okay. By the way, what should I eat? I love hotpot, but I heard it is not good for health.
Hotpot is delicious, but it is too hot if you eat it every day. You can try adding more leafy greens like bok choy. In addition, try to eat some tofu instead of just meat. It balances the diet.
I will try that. Do I need to see a TCM doctor first before starting these things?
Yes, of course. A doctor can check your pulse and decide what herbs you need. For example, if your tongue is pale, you might need different tea than if it is red. It is safer to ask first.
That makes sense. Where can I find a good clinic near the Wuhua area?
There is a famous old shop on Minjiang Road. It has been open for thirty years. The doctors there know many traditional recipes. You can walk there early in the morning since the air is fresh.
Great. Thank you for your advice, Health Coach. I will go there next week.
You're welcome, Wei Ming. I hope you feel better soon. Remember, balance is key. If you have more questions, just call me. Oh, and drink plenty of water!

messages.content: Hi Li Ming, I'm feeling a bit stressed today. My son, Xiao Le, just told me he wants to study art in Kunming instead of engineering here in Chengdu.

Oh no, I can understand why you're worried. To be honest, I remember my own son wanting to do something different last year. Well, it's always hard when children make big choices that aren't what we expected.
Exactly. I worked very hard in the engineering field since I graduated. But Xiao Le says he loves painting since he was five years old. Do you think he should listen to me?
Actually, maybe you should listen to him a little more. Although engineering is stable, art is a passion. Have you seen his paintings? They are really good, you know.
I have seen them, but they are not enough for a university. In China, parents usually want their children to have a good job. What would you do if your child wanted to go to a small university?
That's a fair point. In Chengdu, many families care about job security. However, I think if he is truly talented, he might succeed. By the way, Kunming has a famous art college, right?
Yes, the Yunnan Academy of Fine Arts is very famous. But the cost of living there is higher. I don't want him to have too much debt when he starts working.

I guess that's a real concern. Actually, you could try to find a scholarship-time job for him first. He can work at a local cafe or a design shop while he studies. That way, he doesn't need to borrow too much money.
That's an interesting idea. But his uncle says he should go to a tech company in Zhongguancun to make more money. I feel confused about what is the right path for him.
Well, different people have different opinions. To be honest, your son is the one who will live that life. If he hates studying art, maybe he will regret it later if he doesn't love it anymore.
You make sense. Maybe I should talk to him again tonight. We usually eat hotpot together on weekends. Do you think cooking together helps us talk?
Of course! Cooking is a great way to relax. You can make some spicy fish hotpot. It is very popular in Sichuan. While you are eating, just ask him gently about his dreams.
Thank you for your advice, Li Ming. I will try to make the hotpot this Sunday. I hope we can solve this problem without fighting.
You're welcome. I think you will do fine. Remember, it's important to support each other. Good luck with the hotpot and the talk!

messages.content: Hi Li Ming, I'm a bit stressed. My son, Xiao Le, wants to quit his math tutoring and learn video editing instead. His teachers are worried he won't pass the Gaokao later.
I totally get why you're worried, Wang Fang. To be honest, it's hard when your child makes a big decision like that. Well, have you talked to Xiao Le about his dreams since he was a teenager?
Yes, but he just said math is boring. He thinks video editing is the future. I guess I am afraid that if he fails the entrance exam, he will lose all his hard work.

That is a very natural feeling for a parent. Actually, many parents in Chengdu feel the same pressure. But you know, the world has changed a lot since we were young. Maybe he can try to do both for a while?
Do you think that is a good idea? I am not sure how to explain it to him without arguing. He thinks I only care about his grades, not his happiness.
Oh, that sounds really tough. I think you should tell him that you love him and want him to be happy, not just successful. By the way, has he shown you any of his video projects lately?
Yes, he made a short film about our family trip to Leshan. It was actually quite good. I watched it last night, but I felt guilty because I didn't support him properly.

You shouldn't feel guilty. Of course, his creativity is impressive. If you watch his work and give him some praise, he might listen more to you. Actually, I remember seeing a similar story in a neighborhood group chat yesterday.
Really? What happened there? I hope we can resolve this conflict before the summer holidays start. I don't want to lose our relationship with him.
Well, in that story, the parent agreed to let the child take a summer course in editing while still taking some math classes. It was a compromise. I guess that could work for Xiao Le too.
That sounds like a reasonable solution. I will try to talk to him this weekend. Thank you for your advice, Li Ming. You are very helpful.
You are welcome! By the way, if you want to cool down, we can go for a walk in Jinniu Park later. The weather is nice today. Let's hope your talk goes well!

messages.content: Hi Aunt Mei! I'm Hua. I've been studying here at Sichuan University for six months since September, and I'm so hungry. Do you have any delicious street food I can try near your stall?

Hi Hua! Oh, welcome to the Old Street night market. Well, you've come to the right place. You know, my family has run this stall for ten years, and we make the best Mapo Tofu and boiled mutton you can imagine. If you're hungry, I think you should try our spicy hot pot; it's famous in Chengdu because the peppers are so fresh.

That sounds amazing, but I can't eat very spicy food. Actually, I've tried spicy food before, but my stomach hurts sometimes. What about less spicy options? Also, how much does a bowl of noodles cost?

Oh, I understand! To be honest, even though we use lots of chili oil, we can make the soup mild if you ask. You know, we have a special fish ball soup that is very tasty but not spicy at all. As for the price, a bowl of our famous Dan Dan noodles is only 15 yuan. That's very cheap compared to the restaurants up near the university gate.

Fifteen yuan is great! I usually order takeout from food delivery apps when I don't have time to cook. But I guess eating here is better because the food is fresh. Can I see the menu, and what should I order if I want something quick?

Yes, look here! We have a big list with photos. You know, many students like our cold tofu because it's ready in two minutes. If you order that, you can walk to your dorm while it cools down. Actually, the cold noodles are also good, but they take a little longer to cool. Which one do you prefer?

I'll take the cold tofu, please. It looks very simple, but I think simple food is the best. By the way, is it polite to drink my soup while eating? Some people say you shouldn't make noise when eating in China.

Haha, no problem! You know, in our family, we always finish the soup because it shows you like the food. Actually, making some noise while drinking soup is normal here; it means the broth is hot and delicious. But you shouldn't talk with your mouth full. That is not polite at all, and I guess you want to avoid that.
Got it. I won't talk with my mouth full. Speaking of money, do you accept WeChat Pay? I don't have enough cash, and I haven't learned how to use the app yet. Is it hard to set up?

Yes, we accept WeChat Pay and Alipay. It's very easy! You just scan the QR code on my phone. Honestly, almost everyone in Chengdu uses phones for everything now. If you don't have the app, I can help you download it, but it takes about five minutes. Do you have a smartphone?

Yes, I have an iPhonePhone phone. It's an iPhone models phone. I've used it for taking photos since last year. Can I pay now, or should I wait until I finish my homework first? I have a test tomorrow.

Oh, you should eat now! You know, it's hard to study on an empty stomach. Actually, you can pay with your phone now, and I'll bring your food to your dorm if you tell me your room number. If you wait, you might be too tired to focus on your test tomorrow. Shall I call a friend to help you later?

That's very kind of you. I will pay now. Thank you for the tip about the soup noise; I didn't know that. I'm really hungry now. Can I have the spicy mutton next time? I think I can handle it after this tofu.

You're welcome! Well, you are very welcome. Of course, you can try the spicy mutton next time. It's a bit hot, but it makes you feel warm when it's autumn like this. I guess you're going to love it. Here is your cold tofu; enjoy it while it's still cold!

messages.content: Hi Auntie Wang, I'm Hua. I've been studying at Sichuan University for two years, but I haven't found a good place to eat yet. Do you know any cheap food stalls near the campus?
Hi Hua! Well, of course I know. You know, my stall is right on Old Street, just a ten-minute walk from the campus gate. Actually, we sell lots of spicy food there, like Mapo Tofu and boiled noodles.
That sounds amazing! I love spicy food, although I sometimes get too hot. Is the tofu very spicy today?

Haha, it's quite spicy, you know. But don't worry, we can add less chili oil if you want. To be honest, I've been making this recipe for twenty years, so I know how to adjust it. Would you like to try a small bowl first?
Yes, please. How much does it cost? I'm trying to save money for my next semester.
It's very affordable. A small bowl is only fifteen yuan, which is less than a taxi ride! In addition, we have other dishes like braised pork or cold beef. You can order whatever you like.
Great. I usually use a food delivery app like Meituan, but sometimes the prices are higher there. Do you use an app too?

Well, I don't use an app because I sell from my own stall. However, many young people order from us through the app because it's convenient. But you know, eating here with me is faster and the food is fresher.
That makes sense. What if I want to eat with my friends later? Should we sit at a table?

Oh, yes! We have a few plastic tables under the big tree. You can sit there if you want. Actually, it's quite popular in the evening, so you should come early. If you come after nine, we might not have space.
I see. When did you start selling here? Did you learn all the cooking skills by yourself?

I started ten years ago, since I wanted to make a living. You know, my grandmother taught me how to make the chili sauce when I was young. So I've been perfecting it ever since. It's nice to see so many students like you come here.
Thank you for sharing your story. I think I'll come here tomorrow evening. Do you have any tips for ordering spicy food?
Well, just tell me how much spice you want, like 'mild', 'medium', or 'super spicy'. Also, try to drink some soy milk to cool your mouth down. I hope you enjoy your meal tomorrow!

messages.content: Hi, I'm Feng Xia. I am planning a trip to a village near Lanzhou next summer. I want to take a long bus ride, but I am not sure how to book the tickets. Can you help me?

Hello, Feng! Well, I think you are in the right place. Actually, I travel a lot along the Yellow River, and I have done many road trips since last year. You can book long-distance buses online using apps like WeChat or Alipay. It's much easier than going to the station.
Oh, I see. But I heard the roads in the countryside are bad. Is it safe if I drive myself? I want to visit a small town called Tongwei.

To be honest, the main highways the highway is very safe and smooth, but the small roads can be a bit rough. If you drive, you should be careful because the speed might be slow there. By the way, Tongwei is a great place! It's famous for its delicious noodles. Have you tried making them before?
No, I have not. I usually eat dumplings in Beijing, but I want to try real local food. What should I do if I get lost? I am worried about the traffic rules in the village.

Don't worry! You know, most villages have clear signs now. If you use a map app, it will guide you easily. Actually, the traffic rules are quite simple: always drive on the right side and stop at red lights. I guess you should also carry some cash, just in case you need to pay for a small taxi.
That sounds good. When I was in Chengdu, the buses were very crowded. Will the buses in Gansu province be empty? I want to have some space for my camera.

Well, it depends on the time. In the morning, the buses are usually full because people go to work. However, if you go in the afternoon, there are many empty seats. You can relax and enjoy the view of the mountains. Do you like taking photos of nature?
Yes, I love nature! I want to take pictures of the Yellow River. Is there a good place near the river where I can stop? I plan to stay there for two days.

Of course! There is a beautiful park right along the river in Lanzhou. You can stop there to see the water flow. It's very peaceful, and you can take your time there. If you stay for two days, you might also want to visit some nearby ancient towns. What kind of hotels do you prefer?
I prefer hotels with hot water and a nice view. Do you know any guesthouses in the village? I heard the prices have gone up a lot since last year.

Yes, the prices have risen quite a bit, especially in the tourist season. Actually, there are some small guesthouses that are cheaper than big hotels. They are often family-run, and the owners are very friendly. You could also stay with a local family if you want a better experience.
That sounds interesting. What if it rains? I am not used to the weather in the north. It was sunny today, but I heard the rain comes quickly.

You know, the weather can change very fast in the summer. If it starts raining, just take an umbrella or wear a raincoat. It's not too bad because the rain usually stops after an hour. In addition, you can still enjoy your trip indoors. Do you have a backup plan if the rain is heavy?
I guess I will buy a tent. I think camping is a good idea. But I am not sure if I can find a good spot. Can you give me some advice?

Well, camping is a great idea if the weather is nice! You can find many open spaces near the river. However, you need to check the rules first. Some villages do not allow camping, but others are very welcoming. I think you should ask the local people about the best place. Have you ever camped before?
No, this will be my first time. I am a little nervous, but I am excited. Thank you for all your help, Liu Li. Your blog is very helpful.

You are welcome! I'm so glad to help. Actually, I think you will have a wonderful time. Just remember to stay safe and enjoy the local food. If you need more tips, feel free to ask. Good luck with your trip to Tongwei!

messages.content: Hi Liu Li. I'm planning a trip to a small village near Lanzhou this summer. I've heard the Yellow River is beautiful.
Hello Feng! That sounds like a great idea. Well, actually, the area around Lanzhou is perfect in summer. You can see the river flowing right through the city. Have you booked your train ticket yet?
No, I haven't. I'm not sure how to book high-speed trains to small towns. The big stations are confusing.

I think you should use the 12306 app. It's the official website, and it works very well since last year. By the way, if you go to a smaller station like Baiyin, the tickets might be cheaper than flying.
Maybe. But I also want to drive my own car to the countryside. Is it easy to rent a car in Lanzhou?

Yes, of course. You can rent a car from places like Hertz Auto Auto, and it's quite popular with tourists now. However, if you drive, you need to be careful because the roads to the villages are sometimes narrow. Actually, you know, public buses are also very convenient there.
That's true. What kind of food should I eat in the Yellow River valley? I love noodles.

You must try Lanzhou beef noodles! They are famous and very delicious. In addition, you can eat some lamb hotpot in the evening. It's a local specialty that you will love. To be honest, it tastes much better than the food I ate in Beijing.
I've never tried hotpot before. Do you think it's too spicy for me? I like mild food.

Well, actually, the hotpot in Lanzhou isn't usually very spicy unless you ask for it. You can choose a clear broth or a tomato base. If you don't like spicy food, you can just tell the waiter. It's quite safe.
Good to know. What should I do if the weather changes suddenly while I am on my road trip?

I guess you should check the weather forecast every day before you leave. Also, if it rains, you can stop in a town like Gansu to stay in a hotel. Many hotels have nice views of the mountains, which is quite relaxing. Have you thought about your accommodation?
Yes, I want to stay in a guesthouse. But I am worried about the price. Is it expensive to travel in rural areas?

Don't worry, it's not that expensive. The prices have gone down since last year. Actually, a simple room can cost only 200 yuan a night. In addition, eating local food is much cheaper than dining in big cities. You will save money.
That makes me feel better. Thank you for your advice. I'll book my train ticket soon.
You are welcome! I hope you have a wonderful trip. If you need more help planning, just ask me. I think you will enjoy the scenery very much.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Lin. I'm sitting at a small table in the corner of this coffee shop on Wuhua Road in Hangzhou. It's a bit cloudy today, so the light is soft. I've been trying to find a part-time job online, but I also need to study for my computer science exams. It's really hard to balance both right now.

Well, I completely understand. Actually, I just switched to a fully remote role at a tech company in Hangzhou last year. To be honest, managing my time has been a big challenge at first. I used to spend six hours on screens just for work, and then I had to study in the evening. But now I try to limit my screen time after 8 PM.

That's good advice. Which online learning platforms do you recommend for computer science? I've been using some English sites, but the prices are too high. I'm thinking of trying a Chinese platform instead.

Oh, that's a great idea. For example, I've been using a local platform called Chaoxing since last semester. It's very popular among university students in Zhejiang province. You can find lots of video lessons for subjects like data structures and algorithms. In addition, the prices are much more affordable than the foreign ones. Have you tried downloading their app yet?

No, I haven't. I guess I should download it this weekend. But I'm also worried about collaborating with colleagues. My boss says we often work with teams in Shenzhen and Beijing. I'm not sure how to communicate effectively with them online.

Actually, it depends on the tools your company uses. In my case, we mostly use DingTalk for meetings and file sharing. It's very common in Chinese tech companies. If you join their team meetings on time and speak clearly, you won't have any problems. Also, many colleagues prefer sending detailed messages via DingTalk instead of calling, so you can write your thoughts down. Do you use DingTalk already?
Yes, I've seen it mentioned a few times. But I feel nervous because I'm not a native speaker. Sometimes I worry that my English isn't good enough for important presentations meetings.

I think you shouldn't worry too much. When I first started working remotely, I was also nervous about speaking in meetings. However, I found that people care more about your ideas than your accent. For example, if you prepare your points in advance, it's easier to explain them clearly. By the way, do you have any upcoming exams that are stressing you out?

Yes, I have a final exam next week on operating systems. I've been reviewing my notes for three days now. I feel a bit tired because I've been studying since morning. I really need a break, but I don't want to fail.

Well, taking a break is important. You know, I remember last year when I was preparing for my finals. I studied non-stop stop for two days, but then my mind went blank during the test. It's better to take a short walk or drink some tea to relax. How about you have some warm soy milk? It helps me concentrate when I'm studying in the evening.

That sounds like a good suggestion. I'll try drinking some soy milk. Actually, I think I will take a walk in the Xixi Wetland Park nearby after I finish this conversation. It's very peaceful there. Maybe I can study a little bit more if the weather is nice.

That's a perfect plan. The air in the wetland is really fresh, and it's a great place to clear your mind. Although it's cloudy today, the evening might be warmer. I guess you should relax a bit more before the exam. If you need any tips on managing screen time or choosing jobs, feel free to ask me anytime.

messages.content: Hi! I'm Qiang. I've been volunteering at the library in Tianhe since last year, and I think it's important for our community. What do you think about these kinds of events?

Well, that's great, Qiang! Actually, I organize many local festivals here in Guangzhou. To be honest, I think volunteering is the best way to know your neighbors better. Have you joined any recent events?
Yes, I helped at a tea festival in Tianhe Park last month. We served oolong tea and made paper cuttings. It was fun! Do you organize festivals in other places too?

Oh, yes! For example, last summer we had a big food fair in a small town called Zhongshan. You know, we invited cooks from different villages to make dim sum and rice noodles. If people want to learn new skills, they come from far away.
That sounds delicious! I guess I would love to try dim sum there. By the way, I'm thinking of voting for the city council next month. Is that a good idea?
Honesty, it's a very good idea! Many residents don't vote, but your voice matters. Actually, if you vote, maybe the transport lines will improve. Do you care about public transport improvements?
Absolutely! The metro in Guangzhou is fast, but sometimes it's too crowded during rush hour. I think more trains or new stations would help people get to work on time.

You're right. I mean, last year we saw a new line open in Shenzhen, and it changed everything. If we vote for better projects, maybe we can see new stations in Tianhe soon. What other topics are you interested in?
I think education is important too. If children have better schools, they will have better jobs in the future. Have you ever volunteered to help children learn English?

Well, we have programs in some schools where volunteers teach English on weekends. Although English isn't easy for everyone, it's useful for traveling. By the way, are you planning to teach or just help with activities?
I just want to help with activities, like reading books to kids. Actually, I haven't done that before, but I like reading. Would you like to come to my library event next week?
That would be wonderful! I think it would be nice to meet some of the children. Oh, and if you want, you can bring some local snacks like mooncakes. They're not for the holiday, but they're tasty!
Sure, I'll bring mooncakes. I'm looking forward to it. Thanks for telling me about the festival in Zhongshan. Maybe I can go there next year with you!

Hi Qiang! That's great. Well, the library volunteers in Tianhe are very helpful. You know, we need more people like you to organize the reading events for kids.
Actually, I would love to help. But I'm busy with work sometimes. If I have time, I'll come on weekends.
That's perfectly fine! To be honest, we understand that many people have jobs. If you can come once a month, that would still make a big difference.
Oh, by the way, do you know about the Dragon Boat Festival next month? We are planning a big race in my neighborhood.
Yes! I've heard about the Dragon Boat Festival in Guangzhou. It's usually very exciting. Did you say the race is in Tianhe? Actually, the crowds there can be huge.
Yes, it is in Tianhe. I think it will be noisy, but the food is delicious. We have zongzi and lotus root soup.
Zongzi and lotus root soup are my favorite foods for that holiday. Well, if you are volunteering, maybe we can help you sell the tickets for the race?
That's a good idea. I haven't thought of that. Also, I'm thinking about voting for the city council soon.
That's a smart decision. You know, voting helps us decide on public transport improvements. For example, we want better buses to the older neighborhoods.
Exactly. The bus line to Baiyun is slow. If the council fixes agrees, the travel time will be much shorter.
I guess that would help many families. By the way, are you free this Saturday? We have a meeting to discuss the new bike lanes in the city.
I'm not sure yet. I have a meeting at 10 AM. But if it starts later, I can join you.
Great! We can start at 11 AM instead. Actually, it might be quicker if you take the metro from Zhujiang New Town. It's less crowded than the taxi.
Okay, I'll take the metro then. Thanks for your help, I really appreciate it.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Wei. I have been working in Beijing since 2018, but it has been hard to visit my family in Kunming this year because of my busy schedule.

Hi Wei, I completely understand. Actually, many people in Beijing feel the same way. Well, have you made any plans for the Mid-Autumn Festival next month? That's an important time for family reunions.
Yes, I think I might go to Kunming if I can get a train ticket. My parents live in Xichuan District, and I want to make mooncakes with them again.

That sounds wonderful. You know, making mooncakes together is a special tradition. Last year, my family made them in our small kitchen in Chengdu. We used lotus seed paste and red bean filling, which are very popular.
Oh, I love red bean filling. But I am worried about the long journey. The train from Kunming to Beijing takes almost two days, and I have a lot of work meetings in September.

To be honest, I guess it's a tough balance between work and family. However, if you miss this festival, you might feel sad for a long time. Actually, why don't you try to finish your projects a week earlier? That way, you can relax on the train.
That is a good idea. I have not done this before, but I will try. Do you think we should call my grandparents in Dali first? They always ask if we have eaten our dinner.
Yes, of course! You should call them as soon as you book the ticket. They are probably waiting for your news. By the way, when you call, tell them you have been missing their cooking since you left.
I will tell them that. But I am also thinking about buying some gifts for my aunt in Harbin. She lives far away, so maybe I can send a package by post office.

That is very thoughtful of you. Sending Actually, sending gifts is a nice gesture, especially for relatives in colder places like Harbin. You could send some fresh fruits from Kunming, like pears, which are delicious in autumn.
Pears are a great idea! I have been thinking about that. If I go to Kunming, will I have enough time to visit my sister's new apartment in Wuhua District?

Well, that depends on your schedule. If you go in the afternoon, you might have a few hours free. Actually, Wuhua is quite far from the old city, but the new apartments there are very modern and quiet.
I think I will try to make it work. I have been working too much, and I need to spend more time with my family. What do you do during the Mid-Autumn Festival?

I usually stay in Beijing since I don't have family here, but I visit my friends in Xiamen by video call. You know, seeing them on the screen feels a bit like being there. Anyway, I hope your trip to Kunming goes well!

messages.content: Hi tutor, I'm Wei. It's late September now and I feel very busy with work in Beijing. I've been working since 8 am every day. Do you know anything about the Mid-Autumn Festival?

Hello Wei! Well, the Mid-Autumn Festival is one of my favorite holidays. Actually, it's always a special time when families get together. You know, it's supposed to be in mid-September September or early October usually. Have you made any plans for this year?

To be honest, I haven't planned much. My schedule is really tight. I work at a company near Haidian and I have meetings every day. But my grandparents live in a small town called Taizhou in Zhejiang. I miss them because they want to see me.

That's so sad. Actually, many people feel the same way, especially those who live in big cities like Beijing. You know, it's really important to visit your grandparents at least once a year. If you could go to Taizhou, I think they would be very happy. Do you plan to take the train?

I think I might try. Last year I took the overnight train from Beijing South to Hangzhou first. It was long but comfortable. Maybe I can go to Taizhou by plane this time? But I need to save money. Oh, and I remember my mom made mooncakes last time.

That sounds great! Well, flying is faster, but the train is more fun if you have time. By the way, mooncakes are delicious, aren't they? You know, there are many kinds, like the ones with lotus seed paste or red bean. Do you like eating them yourself, or do you prefer buying them from shops?

I like eating them, but I also enjoy making them with my family. Last week, I helped my mom buy ingredients at a market in Wangfujing. We were mixing the filling and wrapping the dough. It was fun because we talked and laughed while we worked. But now I am too busy to do that.

Oh, that's wonderful! Actually, making mooncakes together is a very special tradition. You know, it helps you remember your family and share good times. I guess you should try to find some time soon. If you make them next month, I think your grandparents would love them very much. Have you ever tried sending them by post?

Yes, I've sent some before. Last year I sent a box to Taizhou since the festival was near. My grandparents were so excited when they opened it. But this year, I am worried because work is very hard. Maybe I can call them instead? I can talk for a long time on WeChat.

That's a good idea, Wei. You know, long-distance calls are very common now, especially during holidays. Actually, hearing their voices is still very important even if you can't visit. To be honest, I think you should call them at least twice before the festival. What time do you usually call them?

I usually call them in the evening, around 7 pm. They are retired now so they have free time. But sometimes I feel bad because they are waiting for me. I wish I could balance work and family better. Do you think people in Beijing understand this problem?

Well, many people in Beijing do understand, I think. You know, life is very fast here, so we all struggle a bit. Actually, your grandparents probably just want to feel close to you. If you call them often, I guess they will feel less lonely. Have you ever thought about asking your boss for some time off next month?

That is a possibility. I haven't asked yet because I am afraid of losing my job. But if I ask politely, maybe I can get two days off. I want to see my parents and help them make mooncakes. It seems like a big decision, but family is very important to me.

You're absolutely right, Wei. Family is everything in China, you know. Actually, most employers understand if you explain it well. I think you should try to ask them. By the way, if you go to Taizhou, you can also visit West Lake on the way. It's beautiful and good for relaxing. What do you think?

messages.content: Hi, my name is Lin. I am planning a trip to Chengdu from Wuhan next weekend. What is the best way to get there?
Hello, Lin! Actually, the high-speed train is the best choice because it is fast and comfortable. You can take the G1067 train from Wuhan to Chengdu. By the way, it usually takes about five hours.
That sounds good. Have you ever taken this train before?
Yes, I have! I took it last autumn since I was visiting my friends in Sichuan. It was very smooth. Although the station is busy, the journey itself is quite relaxing.
I want to book my ticket online. Where should I go? Do I need to go to the station?

You don't need to go to the station if you book in advance. You can use apps like 12306 or Trip.com. However, sometimes there are too many people online, so you might need to try again later if the tickets are sold out.
I see. I am worried about the crowds. Is it crowded at the train station?

To be honest, Chengdu East Railway Station is very crowded during holidays. But since you are going on a weekday evening, it should be better. If you arrive early, you can find a seat before the rush.
Okay. I prefer a seat with a window. Is it hard to get one?

Well, it depends on which train car you choose. The second-class seats have windows, and if you book a seat with the number ending in 0 or 4, you usually get a window seat. It's not difficult if you book online.
Great. What can I eat during the trip? I want to try something local.
There is a dining car on the train where you can eat. You can try hot pot soup or mapo tofu from there. Also, many students buy snacks from the small shops in Chengdu before they get on the train.
That sounds delicious! Do I need to bring my own water?

Actually, there are water fountainsling machines on the train, but you can bring your own bottle. Also, remember to bring some snacks like rice cakes or dried fruit because the dining car might be crowded.
Thank you very much for your advice. I feel much better now.
You are welcome! I hope you have a wonderful time in Chengdu. You can visit Wenshu Monastery or enjoy some spicy food there. Let me know if you have any other questions.

Thank you for your help. I feel more confident now about my trip.
You're welcome! Just remember to arrive at the station early. If you get there too late, you might miss the train.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Ming. I'm a fresh graduate from Nanjing University. I have been looking for a marketing job since last month, but I am not sure which company to choose. Do you think I should apply to a big firm in Jiangning?

Well, that's a great question, Ming. Actually, Nanjing University is very famous, so your resume should be strong. In addition, big firms in Jiangning often have better training programs. Have you written your resume yet, or are you still working on it?

I have finished my resume, but I am worried about the interview. I know I need to speak confidently, but sometimes I get nervous. What if the interviewers ask difficult questions about my past projects?

To be honest, it is normal to feel nervous before an interview. You know, most people feel the same way. If the interviewers ask difficult questions, just try to explain your ideas clearly. For example, you can say what you learned from every project, even if there were some problems.
That makes sense. By the way, I also want to ask about work-life balance. I heard that some companies in China work very long hours. Is it possible to have a healthy life if I join a big company?

Oh, that is a very important point. Actually, the situation varies from company to company. Some big firms expect you to work overtime, but others respect your personal time. You should ask about this during the interview. If you ask them how they handle work-life balance, it shows that you care about your health.
Good idea. I will ask them about that. Also, I am thinking of moving to Hangzhou because the weather is nice there in autumn. Do you think it is a good place to find a marketing job?

Hangzhou is actually a wonderful city, especially in autumn. The weather is pleasant, and there are many tech and e-commerce companies there. However, the cost of living is higher than in Nanjing. If you are willing to move, you could look at neighborhoods near West Lake, where many young professionals live.
I guess I should weigh the pros and cons. Maybe I can take a weekend train to Hangzhou to visit some companies. What kind of food should I try there? I have never been to Hangzhou before.

That's a smart plan! You can visit some offices on a weekend trip. As for food, you must try the famous Dongpo Pork. It is delicious and very popular. In addition, you can enjoy the local tea at a small shop near the West Lake. It would be a nice way to relax before making a decision.
Dongpo Pork sounds amazing! I will try it. But I am still confused about whether to accept an offer from Nanjing or Hangzhou. My family lives in Nanjing. Do you think I should stay close to them?

That's a difficult decision, Ming. You know, being close to your family is very important in China. If you stay in Nanjing, you can help them and visit them often. Although Hangzhou has great opportunities, the distance might make you miss them. I think you should consider how much you miss your family when you make your final choice.
You are right. I will call my parents tonight and ask their opinion. Thank you very much for your advice. I feel much more confident now about applying for jobs.

You're very welcome! Actually, taking time to think is the best thing you can do. I hope you get a great job offer soon. If you need more help with your resume or interview preparation, just let me know. Good luck with everything!

messages.content: Hi, I'm Ming. I've just graduated from Nanjing University and I'm looking for a marketing job. Actually, I've been sending resumes since last week, but I haven't got any replies yet.

Well, congratulations on your graduation! That's a big step. To be honest, the job market can be very competitive right now, so don't worry too much. Have you tailored your resume specifically for marketing roles, or do you think it's a bit generic?
I think it's a bit generic. I wrote it last month while I was studying for my final exams. I used my project at the Confucius Temple as an example, but I'm not sure if that's clear enough.

That's a great idea. You know, a specific project shows your practical skills better than just listing courses. If I were you, I'd highlight the results, like how many people visited your event. Actually, do you have any experience with digital platforms, like WeChat Official Accounts?
Yes, I managed the WeChat account for my university club. We have about five thousand followers. But I'm worried about the interview. What if the interviewer asks difficult questions?

Oh, that's a good number! That sounds impressive. Most interviewers want to know if you can handle pressure. If an interviewer asks you a difficult question, try to stay calm and think for a moment. You could say, 'Let me consider that for a second.' Have you prepared any common questions, like 'Tell me about yourself'?
I've prepared a short answer about my study at Nanjing University. But I'm also thinking about the work-life balance. Do you think the companies in Nanjing are strict?

Actually, it depends on the company. Some big firms in the business district near the Confucius Temple can be quite busy, especially during the busy season. However, many modern companies try to respect personal time. By the way, did you check if they offer flexible hours or remote work options?
I haven't checked that yet. I'm a bit worried about the salary, too. Is the starting salary for a fresh graduate usually high in Nanjing?

Well, the starting salary varies a lot. For a fresh graduate, it might not be as high as you expect, maybe around three thousand to six thousand RMB per month. But in addition to the salary, you should ask about benefits like health insurance and paid leave. What kind of food do you usually eat after work? Maybe you can try a local snack shop if you're nearby.

I love eating dumplings! But I guess I need to focus on the job first. If I get a good offer, I will accept it quickly. Do you think I should apply to companies in other cities, like Shanghai or Beijing?

That's a big decision. Moving to Shanghai or Beijing could give you more opportunities, but the cost of living is much higher there. If you stay in Nanjing, you might have a better work-life balance. Actually, you could apply to companies in both places to see what happens. Which neighborhood in Nanjing would you prefer to live in?
I think I'd like to live in Xuanwu Lake area. It's quiet and near the university. I'll finish updating my resume today. Thank you for your advice, coach.

You're welcome! Xuanwu Lake is a lovely place, and it's great for relaxing after work. Well, I think you have a solid plan now. Just remember to practice your interview answers out loud. Good luck with the applications, Ming! I hope you find a great job soon.

messages.content: Hi Li, it is Saturday afternoon and I am so free. I have been wanting to do something new this weekend.
Well, that sounds nice! You know, I have been thinking about playing table tennis recently. Actually, there is a great club near my office in Chaoyang District.
Wow, I have never played before. Is it hard for beginners? I am a bit afraid I will make mistakes.
Don't worry, it is actually quite easy to start. The coaches are very patient. If you go there, you will probably meet many people who like sports too.
That is good. But I also like quiet activities. Maybe reading local newspapers is better for me?
Oh, that is a great idea. There is a small bookshop in Haidian that sells many old newspapers. You can sit there and read for an hour. It is very peaceful.
I guess I should visit a cultural center instead. Do you know any good places in smaller towns?
Of course! You should try Wuzhen in Zhejiang Province. It is a beautiful town with many cultural centers. There have been lots of art exhibitions there since last month.
Wuzhen sounds amazing. But I am thinking about cooking traditional snacks at home this evening.
That is a wonderful choice. You can make some delicious mooncakes or osmanthus cakes. The smell fills the whole kitchen, and your neighbors will probably come over.
Actually, I want to try the osmanthus cakes. They are sweet and soft. Where can I buy the ingredients?
You can find them at the market near Wangfujing Street. The ingredients are fresh, and the shop owner is very helpful. You will definitely enjoy making them.
Thank you for your suggestions, Li. I think I will cook the snacks first and then maybe visit the market.
That sounds like a perfect plan. To be honest, cooking is the best way to relax after work. Have fun, and let me know if you need any recipes later!

messages.content: Hi Li, it's Wei. I've been thinking about my weekend hobbies since this morning. What do you usually do to relax after work?
Hello Wei! To be honest, I usually play table tennis at the community center near the park. Actually, I've been playing there for three years since I moved to Beijing. Have you tried it before?
I have tried it, but I haven't played in a while. I was playing in Chengdu when I was younger. Do you think I need a partner if I want to join you?
Well, it's very important to have a partner for table tennis. You can't really practice alone. If you don't have one, I can find someone for you. Actually, many people play in teams at weekends.
That sounds good. Besides sports, I like reading local newspapers. I often read about culture in the Dongcheng District. Do you read news too?

Yes, I read the news every morning. Well, I prefer to read online on my phone because it's faster. But sometimes I go to the library near Nanluoguxiang to read old books. Have you been to that library?
I've never been there, but I know the area is very busy. I guess I should visit it next week. What do you think of the food there?
The food is amazing! There's a famous snack shop near the entrance who sells traditional jianbing. You know, if you go on a weekend, it will be crowded. You should go early in the morning.
That's a great idea. Maybe we can cook some snacks together later this month. I like cooking dumplings. Have you cooked Chinese food recently?
Of course! I cooked spicy hotpot last week with my family. It was delicious. In addition, we can learn how to make osmanthus cakes together. They are very popular in autumn. Do you like sweet snacks?
Yes, I love sweet snacks! Osmanthus cakes sound perfect for the season. If we cook them, I will bring the eggs. What other places would you suggest for this weekend?
Actually, we can also visit a cultural center in Tangshan if you have time. There's an exhibition about local history there. It's quite relaxing. What do you think, is it worth visiting?
I think it's a good idea. Although I am busy on Sunday, I might go on Saturday afternoon. How about you? Will you play table tennis or read?
I'll definitely play table tennis this Saturday. Maybe we can play first and then go to the cultural center later. You know, it would be great to spend the whole day together. Let's make a plan soon!

messages.content: I've been reading about the train to Tibet, but honestly, I'm worried about the altitude sickness. I've never been high up before, and I heard it can be really bad.

Actually, that's a very common concern. Many people feel sick when they first go to Lhasa. However, the train helps because you go up slowly, which is better than flying. You can also take some medicine before you leave, just to be safe.
That makes sense. If I take medicine, will it stop me from feeling anything at all? I want to enjoy the trip, but I don't want to feel dizzy.

Well, the medicine won't stop you from feeling anything completely, but it will make it much easier. You might still feel a little tired, but you won't get really sick. By the way, the train has special oxygen masks too, so people can breathe if they need to.
Oh, that's great. Do you think I should bring any special food? I'm not used to eating plain bread and meat, which is what I heard you eat up there.

I think you should bring some snacks from home, like dried fruit or chocolate, because it's good to keep your energy up. Although, don't worry too much about the local food. The butter tea and Tibetan noodles are delicious, and many tourists love them.
I'm curious about the scenery. Since we are taking the train for so long, are there any stops where we can get off and take photos? I really want to see the mountains.

There are a few scenic spots along the way, but the train usually stops only at the big stations like Lanzhou or Xining. Although, you can see amazing views of the Qilian Mountains and the Tibetan plateau from your window. Some people even set up cameras on the train to take pictures!
That sounds exciting. When did you start planning your trip? I'm thinking of going next summer, but I don't know if the tickets are that hard to get.

I started planning about three months ago. You should book your tickets as soon as possible, because they sell out very quickly. In addition, the prices are quite high during the summer holidays, so if you wait until last minute, you might pay more.
Okay, I'll book them early. One last question: is it safe to travel on the train at night? I'm a bit nervous about sleeping in a strange place with so many strangers.

To be honest, it is very safe. The train staff checks everyone's ticket, and the compartment is quite private. You can sleep comfortably in a four-bed room without worrying. I've taken the train many times, and I've never felt unsafe.

messages.content: Hi, I'm planning a trip to a hot spring resort in Zhangjiajie next month. I've heard about the local herbal steam baths there. What kind of herbs do they usually use in the steam bath?

Oh, that sounds like a wonderful idea! Actually, Zhangjiajie is famous for its natural hot springs. To be honest, they often use herbs like mugwort and chrysanthemum to make the steam even more relaxing. You know, these herbs have been used for centuries to improve circulation. Have you ever tried a steam bath with herbs before?
No, not really. I usually just go to the gym in my hometown. But I think it would be interesting. Do you think it's better than drinking herbal tea for fitness?

Well, it depends on what you want to achieve. For example, drinking tea with goji berries and astragalus is great for boosting your energy over time. But the steam bath can help you relax your muscles quickly after a long day. In addition, combining both methods might be the best solution. Do you exercise regularly?
Yes, I run about five kilometers every morning. But lately, my knees have been hurting a bit. Maybe the steam bath could help with that?

That makes sense. Actually, heat therapy can reduce pain and stiffness in the joints. If you go to a place like Wuzhen in Zhejiang, they often have special steam rooms for people with joint issues. Although, you should probably consult a doctor first to be safe. Have you seen a traditional Chinese medicine doctor recently?
I haven't seen one for a while. I guess I should go to see one before my trip. What should I ask them?

You know, you can ask them about your diet as well. For instance, eating more ginger and scallions in your daily meals might help warm your body and protect your knees. Also, ask if there are any specific exercises you should avoid while your knees are sore. What kind of food do you usually eat?
I mostly eat rice, pork, and vegetables. Sometimes I drink soy milk. Do you think I'm eating enough to support my running?

It's a good start, but I think you might need more protein. Actually, adding some tofu or chicken to your diet could be very helpful. For example, eating a bowl of wonton soup with lean meat would give you the strength you need. By the way, did you try acupuncture? It's often recommended alongside diet changes.
I've heard about it, but I'm a bit nervous. Is it painful? I don't want to feel scared during my trip.

Don't worry! To be honest, most people don't feel much pain unless they are very anxious. The needles are very thin, and many clinics use disposable ones for safety. In fact, I have a friend who went to a clinic in Guilin and said it felt like a gentle massage massage. If you are still unsure, you could try a short session just to test it out. How does that sound?
That sounds reasonable. Maybe I will try a short session when I get to Zhangjiajie. Thanks for all your advice!

You are welcome! Actually, combining a healthy diet, regular exercise, and maybe some traditional treatments like acupuncture or herbal steam could really help you recover. I hope your trip goes well and your knees feel better soon. Good luck with your plans!

messages.content: Hi, I'm actually looking for a place to run my morning jogs, not really volunteering. Do you know where the ground is cleanest in this neighborhood?

Well, I think the square near the old pagoda in the Xixi area is perfect for running. We have been cleaning it every weekend since March, so the grass is very tidy now. Although there are some other parks, this one has less traffic.
That's great news. I've heard the air quality is better there, too. But who organizes the cleaning team? I don't want to join if I have to commit too much time.

Actually, it's a small group of residents who meet once a month. You don't have to join the whole team if you just want to run. For example, we usually work for two hours and then take a break. If you like the environment, you can come and see us next Saturday.
I guess I could come then. My schedule is usually busy until 6 PM, but maybe I can make it. What exactly do you do during those two hours?

We mostly pick up trash and water the flower beds. It's not hard work, but it helps a lot because many people leave bottles on the ground. To be honest, the most important thing is keeping the public space safe and clean for everyone.
I see. So it's more about maintaining the area than a big project. Do you coordinate with the property management or the government?

Yes, we work with them. Last year, they gave us some tools and helped us plan the schedule. Although we do most of the work ourselves, their support makes it much easier. In addition, other neighbors often bring snacks for us after the cleaning.
That sounds like a nice community spirit. If I come next Saturday, should I bring anything specific? I have a pair of running shoes, but nothing else.

You're good with your shoes, but maybe bring a bag for the trash you might find. We don't need you to carry heavy bags, just a small one. Also, if you bring some fruit or water, that would be very kind for the other volunteers who have been working since early morning.
I'll definitely bring a bag then. Thank you for explaining. By the way, how long has this volunteer group been active in this suburb?

We started about five years ago. Since then, many members have changed, but the group is still strong. I've been here for two years now, and I really enjoy seeing the square look better every year. It makes me feel proud to live here.
That's inspiring. I think I'll stop by next Saturday just to watch for now. Maybe I'll join in later if I like it.
That's a great idea. You can just arrive when you are free. Well, it's not too late to start enjoying the clean air and the nice path. See you next Saturday then!

messages.content: Hi Tao! I'm Wei. I've been planning to take the high-speed train from Guilin to Yangshuo next weekend. Have you gone there before?
Hi Wei! Yes, I've gone there many times since last year. Actually, it's one of my favorite trips. The scenery along the way is amazing if you look out the window.
That sounds great. But I'm worried because I don't know how to book tickets in advance. Is it hard to buy them on the app?
Oh, don't worry. It's very easy. You just open the 12306 app, choose the date, and that's it. However, you must book early, because the tickets sell out quickly during holidays.
I see. When does the train usually leave? I think I want to arrive early in the afternoon so I can eat lunch.
Well, there are many times, but a good one leaves Guilin around 10 am and arrives in Yangshuo at 11 am. In addition, the trip is only about an hour, so it's very fast.
Perfect! By the way, what should I eat when I get there? I really want to try local Guilin rice noodles.
To be honest, Guilin rice noodles are the best! You should go to a small shop on the way to the Yulong River. The noodles are fresh and spicy, which is delicious.
Spicy is good for me. Do I need a reservation for the river boat ride as well?
Yes, you do. Most boats leave in the early afternoon. If you miss the last boat, you might have to wait until the next day, which is not fun.
Okay, I will book everything this week. What should I wear? It's autumn, right?
It's autumn, so the weather is cool. You should bring a light jacket and comfortable shoes, because you'll walk a lot near the Li River.
Great advice. If it rains, can I still visit the karst mountains?
Actually, the rain makes the mountains look even greener and more beautiful. However, you should take an umbrella, just in case the wind is too strong.
Thanks, Tao! I'll pack my bag now. Have a nice day!
You're welcome, Wei! I hope you have a wonderful trip. See you in Guilin!

messages.content: Hi Tao, I'm planning a trip to Guilin next week. I have heard that taking the high-speed train to Yangshuo is a great idea. Have you ever done this?
Hi Wei! Yes, I have. Actually, I have taken the train since last autumn. It's very fast and the scenery along the way is amazing. You know, the mountains look like green waves when it rains.
That sounds beautiful. But I am worried about booking the tickets. They must be very popular. When should I book them?
Well, you are right. Tickets sell out quickly, especially for weekends. I usually book them about two weeks in advance. If you wait too long, you might not find a seat that is not crowded.
Okay, I will book them soon. The journey takes about two hours. What do you think I should do during that time? Just read a book?
Not necessarily! You should look out the window. Although it is short, the Li River views are worth it. Also, if it rains, the mist makes the karst peaks look like a painting.
I agree. I love pictures. When we arrive in Yangshuo, do we walk to the village or take a taxi? I think walking is better.
Walking is a good idea if you have enough energy. By the way, the path from the station to the old town is quite flat. However, if you buy some Guilin rice noodles for lunch, you might feel tired.
Oh, I forgot about the food. Guilin rice noodles are famous. Have you tried them in Yangshuo before?
Yes, I have! To be honest, they are delicious. The noodles are thin and the soup has a special flavor. There is a small shop near the West Street that makes the best ones.
That sounds tasty. I want to try them. Do I need to know Chinese to order them? I am a bit nervous about speaking.
Don't worry! Most people can point at the menu. Also, many shops have pictures of the dishes. You can just say, 'I want this one.' It's very easy.
Great, that makes me feel better. I think I will order the spicy ones. Do you like spicy food?
I guess I do, but not too much. I prefer the regular version. Maybe you should try both? You can enjoy the heat, but you know, your stomach might get used to it later.

messages.content: Hi Jiang, I'm Lin. I'm looking for some good Longjing tea to buy for my family. Have you seen any good shops around here?

Hello Lin! Well, you are in the right place because Fuchun Street is famous for silk and tea. Actually, there is a small market just down the road where the farmers sell fresh Longjing tea. It's very good since they harvest it this morning.
That sounds nice. But I'm worried about the price. Is it expensive to buy from the market?

To be honest, it depends. The tea can be pricey, but you can negotiate the price if you buy a lot. I've bought tea there before, and the seller always lowers the price if you ask nicely. You know, it's better than buying from a big shop.
Okay, I think I will try to negotiate. By the way, I also need a silk hanfu for a festival. Do you have any silk fabrics here?

Yes, of course! We are lucky to have many silk shops in Hangzhou. Actually, the fabric in Hangzhou is softer than anywhere else in China. If you want a blue one, I can take you to a shop that has many colors. The quality is excellent.
Great. But I'm not sure how to check the quality. Can you teach me?

Well, it's easy. You can burn a small piece of the fabric to see the smoke. If the smell is like burning hair, it's real silk. Although, I guess you should be careful not to burn too much because you don't want to ruin the cloth. Do you want to try it now?
Yes, let's try it. Also, what time do the shops usually close? I need to visit a few places.

Most shops close at six in the evening, but the market stays open until eight. Since it's spring, the weather is warm and pleasant, so you can walk comfortably. In addition, you can take the bus to Xixi Wetland if you have more time. It's very beautiful.
That's a good idea. I'll buy the tea and the fabric today. Thank you for your help, Jiang.
You're welcome, Lin. I'm happy to help. By the way, if you buy the tea now, I will give you a free silk bag to carry it. It's a small gift, but I think you will like it. Let's go to the market now!

messages.content: Hi Jiang. I am looking for good Longjing tea for my family. Do you know where I can find it?

Hello Lin! Well, I am happy to help. Since you want real Longjing tea, you should go to Xixi Wetland Market. Actually, that place has many shops selling fresh tea. But the prices there are a bit high, you know.
I think it is expensive. Maybe I can go to Fuchun Street instead? I have heard the tea here is cheaper.

That is a good idea. Fuchun Street is famous for traditional tea and silk. In addition, the shop owners here are friendly, so they might give you a better price. I bought a box last month and it was very good.
Oh, really? I will try that. But I do not know how to check the quality. Is there something special I should look for?

Yes, of course. You should look for leaves that are flat and green. Also, the tea should smell like chestnuts. If the smell is not right, it is not good quality. I think you should ask the shopkeeper to make a small pot for you first.
Thank you. By the way, I also want to buy a silk sar for my mother. Do you sell good silk here?
Yes, we have many silk items here! Actually, Fuchun Street is the best place in Hangzhou for this. The silk is soft and bright. You know, my grandmother always wore a silk jacket like that.
That sounds nice. I will ask the price now. But I am worried about the cost. Is it too much?

It depends on the quality. A simple one is not expensive, but a fine one can be dear. However, if you buy from me, I can give you a discount because you are a friend. I think your mother will love it.
Really? That is great. If I buy today, can you give me a special price for the tea and the jacket?
Of course! If you buy both things, I can make a good deal for you. Actually, it is better to buy together. You will save some money, and the quality is guaranteed. I hope you like it.
I am sure I will like it. Thank you very much, Jiang. I will go to your shop now.
You are welcome! Come in whenever you want. Oh, by the way, it is very nice today. The weather is perfect for drinking tea. Let's enjoy your shopping!

messages.content: Hi Chen, I'm Zhang. I have been having back pain since last month. It is really bad.

Hello Zhang. Well, I'm sorry to hear that your back hurts so much. Actually, many people in Jinjiang District have similar problems because they sit at desks all day. Can you tell me more about where it hurts?
It is on my lower back. It hurts when I stand up or when I sit too long. I think I stay at my office in Renmin Road.
That makes sense. The Renmin Road area is busy, so sitting for hours must be hard on your body. Since you started having pain last month, have you tried taking any medicine or resting?
I took some pills, but they don't work. I guess my back is very stiff. I felt tired yesterday afternoon.
To be honest, pills might not be enough for stiff muscles. In Traditional Chinese Medicine, we often use cupping therapy. It helps move the energy in your body. Would you like to try it today?
Cupping? I have never done that before. Is it painful? I am a bit scared.

Oh, don't worry. It feels a little warm and sticky, but it isn't very painful. You know, many office workers like it because it relaxes the back quickly. We can start with just three cups if you are nervous.
Okay, I will try it. But it is cold outside. Do I need to wear a thick coat?

Yes, winter in Chengdu can be damp and chilly. Please wear a warm jacket, but take it off when we are inside the clinic. By the way, after the treatment, I recommend eating something hot to keep your body warm.
What food is good? I like spicy food. Should I eat hot pot?

That's a great idea! Hot pot is perfect because it is very hot and warming. You can add beef and tofu to help your digestion. Actually, you could go to a restaurant near the Kunlun Road subway station if you are hungry.
I will go to a hot pot place. How long will the treatment take? I have work tomorrow morning.
The cupping session takes about forty minutes, so you will have enough time. If you feel better, you can come back next week. I hope your back feels less painful soon.

messages.content: Hello, I'm Zhang. I've had back pain since last month, and I think it's because I sit too much at work.
Hi Zhang, I'm Chen. That's actually quite common for office workers. Well, have you tried to rest more, or did you keep working?
I kept working. I think if I stop now, my boss will be angry. But the pain is getting worse, especially in the evening.
I understand, but your health is important. You know, we can try some cupping therapy here. It uses suction small cups to pull out bad energy from your back.
Cupping? What is that? I've never tried it. Is it painful? I guess I'm a bit scared.
Don't worry, it's not very painful. Actually, it might feel a bit like a strong massage suction suction suction suction, but you'll feel relaxed after. You can lie down on the soft mat.
Okay, let's try. By the way, can we eat something afterwards? I'm very hungry now.
Of course! We should eat something warm to help your back. You know, a hot pot with lamb and vegetables is perfect for winter.
Lamb hot pot? I love hot pot! But I don't want to get too full. What do you recommend?
I think a small pot with clear broth is best. You can add tofu and mushrooms, which are good for your body. It's warm and won't upset your stomach.
That sounds good. If I eat that, will my back pain go away quickly?
It might help a lot if you keep doing this treatment. However, it won't fix everything in one day. You need to rest more too.
I will try to rest. Thank you, Nurse Chen. I feel much better just talking to you.
You're welcome, Zhang. You're doing great. Let's go to the kitchen and prepare your hot pot now. It's almost time!

messages.content: Hi Liu, I am so excited because we have finally moved into our new apartment in Xuanwu District.
That is wonderful news! Well, I have been renovating my flat in the same neighborhood for about a year, and it has been a bit tiring but worth it.
Oh, I heard your construction was very loud. It is hard to work on it since you live in an old house.
Exactly! The noise was terrible last summer, but actually, the workers finished everything last week. It is much quieter now.
Do you think we should start our renovation now? We want to make the kitchen look more modern.
You could start soon, but I think you should wait until autumn because the dust will be less annoying. Also, materials are cheaper now compared to last year.
My neighbor told me the cost is very high. He said he spent a lot of money on new furniture.
To be honest, costs vary a lot. My friend bought some old Chinese-style tables and chairs, and they look great without spending much money.
That is a good idea. Do you prefer the old style or the modern one?
I prefer the old style because it fits the history of Xuanwu District. However, if you like modern things, you can choose what you want.
We are worried about the noise again. Is it safe to have construction near our home?
It is usually safe if you choose a reliable company. I had to protect my windows with curtains, but it was not too dangerous.
Maybe we will hire a local team then. Thanks for your advice, Liu!
No problem. By the way, have you tried the local dumplings near your new building? They are very delicious.

messages.content: Hi Liu, I've been renovating my apartment in Xuanwu District for a month now. It's been busy, but we're almost done. How about you? Did you finish your renovation?

Hello Fang! Yes, I finished my flat last week. Actually, it took me three months because the old walls were very thick. You know, the workers were noisy all the time, especially yesterday when they were drilling. How is your project going?
It's noisy, I admit. We had to stop painting last Friday because of the construction. But I think it's worth it. How much did it cost you? I guess I need to compare my budget with yours.

To be honest, it was quite expensive. I spent about 80,000 RMB because I changed the old windows and installed a new kitchen. By the way, did you hire a professional team or do it yourself? If you hire them, the price is usually higher, but the work is faster.
We hired a team from a local company. The manager said it would be cheap, but the price went up since last month. I'm thinking of buying some furniture now. Do you prefer modern or old style?

I prefer a mix, you know. I kept some old wooden furniture because it looks traditional, but I bought a new sofa which is very comfortable. Actually, modern furniture is easier to clean. What about you? Do you want something simple or traditional?
I like traditional style, like the old tables in the shop. But my wife wants a modern kitchen. It's a bit difficult to decide. The noise from your work is still a problem, though. Did it stop today?

I'm sorry about the noise. The drilling stopped this morning, but they are still painting the hallway. If you can wait a few more days, the main noise will be gone. By the way, have you tried the dumpling shop on Jiangning Road? It's open on weekends, and the food is delicious.

Oh, I haven't tried that place. Maybe we can go there after you finish painting. I'd love to eat some real Jiangnan dumplings. Also, I found a small shop in the neighborhood that sells old furniture. It's very nice.

That sounds great! Actually, I visited that shop yesterday. The owner was very friendly and showed me some old chairs which are perfect for the living room. I think you will find something good there. Would you like to go together next Saturday?
Yes, that would be perfect. We can look at the chairs and then have lunch. I guess we can avoid the construction noise if we go in the afternoon. Thanks for the advice, Liu.

You're welcome! It's always better to visit in the afternoon when the workers take a break. I hope your renovation is finished soon. In addition, if you need help choosing the chairs, let me know. I have some ideas about the colors.
