messages.content: Hello, I'm Li Xiao from Beijing. I've never eaten local food before. What should I try?
Well, welcome to Lijiang! You should definitely try our steamed buns with pork filling. They are hot and very soft. By the way, it's quite cold this winter morning, so the steam helps.
Oh, I see. I've been looking for something warm since I arrived yesterday. Are the dumplings here famous too?
Yes, actually our dumplings are famous in Yunnan. I made them myself every morning for ten years. You know, if you want something spicy, I can make them with chili oil.
That sounds delicious. Do you have any drink to go with it? I usually drink coffee, but I don't know if it is available here.
You know, coffee is rare here, but we have amazing sweet is tea! It comes from the Naxi people. It's perfect with hot food. I think you will love the taste.
I've heard of it before. Is it expensive? I only have 50 RMB for breakfast. Can I afford both?
Don't worry, it's very cheap. A bowl of is tea is only 3 RMB, and the buns are 5 RMB. So you can easily buy both with your money. In addition, it is much healthier than coffee.
Okay, that is a good deal. I guess I will order one bowl of tea and two buns. How will I pay?
Well, we accept cash or Alipay. It's very convenient. Oh, by the way, you should eat quickly because many tourists come here early. It can be crowded soon.
I understand. I will pay with my phone. Thank you for your help. I am really hungry now.
You're welcome! Here's your order. It's ready. Enjoy your meal! I hope you have a great time visiting the Old Town.
Thanks! I will tell my friends back in Beijing about this place. See you later.
Of course! Come back anytime if you want more is tea. Goodbye!

messages.content: Hi, I'm Li Xiao from Kunming. I've been visiting Lijiang for two weeks since I arrived last month. I'm really hungry now.
Oh, welcome to Lijiang! Actually, you're in the right place for breakfast. It's cold this winter morning, but my stall is warm. What do you want to eat?
I would like some jiaozi. Do you have them here? I know you have many different types of dumplings in China.
Of course! We have fresh jiaozi made every morning. In fact, many people order them with soy sauce. However, some tourists prefer the spicy one. Which kind do you like?
I think I'll have the regular ones. Are they ready yet?
Well, they're almost done. While I boil them, I can make you some tea. You know, people say Lijiang tea is very famous. It's a great way to start the day.
That sounds nice. Can I have a cup of cha?
Sure thing. By the way, I also have steamed buns called mantou. They are soft and sweet. Would you like to try some with your jiaozi?
Yes, please. Actually, I've never had mantou before. How expensive is it?
It's very cheap, honestly. For about ten yuan, you can have a big bowl of noodles or two jiaozi and some tea. It's a good price for such tasty food.
Ten yuan? That's perfect. I'll take two jiaozi and the mantou.
Great choice. Your food is ready now. Please, sit here while you wait. To be honest, it's cold outside, so this small table is comfortable.
Thank you very much. It's delicious, especially the jiaozi. Have you been selling food here for a long time?
I've been doing this for twenty years since I opened my first shop. In addition, I'm happy to see so many guests from other cities. Enjoy your meal!

messages.content: Hi Auntie Mei, I've been making dumplings since this morning for tonight's dinner. How's the fish soup coming along?

Well, actually, the fish soup is almost ready. I've been boiling the sea bass bass fish in the pot for over an hour because it needs to be clear and fresh. To be honest, I think your dumplings will be the best part of the meal!
I'm so excited. My dad said the first one I make will be lucky for the new year. By the way, have you started preparing the sticky rice cakes yet?

Yes, I've been chopping the mung beans since yesterday afternoon. Actually, we still need to wrap them in bamboo leaves before steaming them. You know, if you help me now, we can finish them before the rain starts later. Do you want to try it?
Sure! I've never wrapped sticky rice cakes before. Is it hard? Also, where did you buy the red fish?

It's not that hard, but it takes practice. I bought the red fish at the wet market near Siming Park this morning because the price was good. Actually, if you watch me carefully, I'm sure you'll do well. Remember to fold the leaves tight so the steam doesn't escape.
Okay, I'll try my best. Did you also buy the ingredients for the braised pork belly yet?

Yes, I've bought the pork and the rock sugar since early morning. To be honest, I think the pork belly will be tender because I've been marinating it with soy sauce and star anise for two hours. By the way, your brother from Beijing is coming tomorrow, right?
Yes, he flies arrived in Xiamen yesterday. He's taking the high-speed train. I guess he's very tired after the long journey.

Oh, he's been traveling for almost twelve hours! Actually, you should prepare some hot tea for him when he gets home. In addition, I've been making a special dessert called 'eight' with longan and glutinous rice. It's a traditional dish in our hometown. Would you like to taste it later?
That sounds delicious. I've always wanted to try longan dessert. Is it sweet?

Well, it's sweet but not too much. You know, my mother used to make it every year, and she said it brings good luck to the family. Actually, if you help me peel the longan, we can finish it before your brother arrives. What do you think?
I'd love to help. Thank you, Auntie Mei. It's so nice to prepare the food with you.

Of course! It's a joy to cook with family. To be honest, I've been waiting for this moment since winter started. Anyway, let's wash our hands and start peeling the longan. I think your brother will be happy to see us working together.

messages.content: Hi Auntie Li! I've been cooking for three hours since morning, but the kitchen is still a bit messy. What should I do first?
Well, you should wash the vegetables first, Wu Fang. Actually, I've been chopping the pork and putting it in the bowl since noon. By the way, did you buy the dried shrimp?
Oh, yes! I bought them last week. But I'm worried about the fish. Do I need to clean it now or later?

You need to clean the fish right now because it smells very strong if you wait. To be honest, my cousin in Zhangzhou always cleans the fish before he marries it with the radish. It tastes much better that way.
That's a good idea. I think I'll clean it now. How many people will come to the dinner tonight? My brother said six, but my sister said eight.

Actually, it's likely eight people if your sister's family comes too. You know, we usually invite the neighbors from the old neighborhood in Gulangyu as well. That makes the table very crowded, but it's very happy.
Oh, really? I guess I should buy more meat. Is duck leg good for this holiday, or should I cook pork?

Both are good, but pork is traditional for the Spring Festival. In the past, we only ate pork and fish for the whole week. Although duck is delicious, my father prefers the red color of the pork. Have you sliced the meat yet?
Not yet, I haven't started. It's hard work! If I finish now, can I watch the fireworks at 8 PM?

Well, you can watch them if you are quick. I've seen the fireworks every year since I was a child. They light up the sky over Xiamen harbor, and it is beautiful. You should also put the dumplings in the fridge if you are not cooking them now.
Okay, I will put them in the fridge. Do you think the weather will be nice for the fireworks? It looks cloudy outside.

I think it might rain lightly, but the fireworks will still be visible. Actually, the rain makes the colors look brighter sometimes. Anyway, let's focus on the food first. Who is going to make the noodle soup?
My mother usually makes it, but she is visiting her friends in Fuzhou. Can I try to make it?

Of course you can! Although you might not make it exactly the same as her, it will be delicious enough. Just remember to add the egg and the green onions. To be honest, the smell of the soup is the best part of the holiday for me.

messages.content: Hi Lin, I am so nervous about my job interview tomorrow. It is for a position in a design firm in Zhongshan.
Well, don't worry too much. I have been in your shoes before, and it is normal to feel this way. Actually, if you have prepared your resume well, you will do great.
I have updated my resume since last month. I added the projects I did at my university in Wuxi. But I am not sure if it is enough.

That sounds like a good start. To be honest, the recruiters in Zhongshan probably look for specific skills, not just a long list. You know, make sure you highlight the part where you used Photoshop or Illustratorllustrator.
Yes, I have used those programs since I started my studies. I think I will mention that in the first paragraph. What about the questions they might ask?

They usually ask about your strengths and weaknesses. For example, they might say, "Can you tell me about a time you faced a problem?" If they ask this, you should think about a real story from your past.
Okay, I have a story about a deadline I missed. I stayed up all night to finish it. I guess I will tell them about that.

Well, that is a bit risky. You know, you should frame it positively. Instead of saying you missed the deadline, say that you learned how to manage your time better since then. It shows you have grown.
Oh, I see. So I should not just say I made a mistake. I have to show I can improve. What do you wear for an interview in Wuhan?

In Wuhan, the weather is still quite cold in late winter, so wear a warm coat but keep your suit or shirt neat. Actually, a dark blue jacket is very professional. You don't want to look too casual with big sneakers.
Good idea. I will bring my own warm coat. Do you think I should bring a snack like a pear or some tea?
No, you do not need to bring food. They have a coffee shop or a tea room nearby. To be honest, drinking a lot of water before the interview makes your mouth dry. Just bring a pen and a notebook.
I have a pen. Thank you for the advice, Lin. I feel a bit calmer now. I hope I can get the job in Zhongsoon.
Of course you will! You have a good resume and you are hardworking. Anyway, just be yourself and talk confidently. I am sure it will work out well for you.

messages.content: Hi Lin. I have been looking for a job since January, but I haven't got any good offers yet. My resume looks a bit old.

Well, don't worry, Huang. Actually, your experience at the Wuhan University library is very impressive. You know, the hiring managers like candidates who have worked in academic places. But maybe you need to update it to show your recent skills.
Yes, I agree. I think the format is not clear. Also, I am worried about the interview next week. What if they ask me difficult questions?

That's normal. To be honest, most interviewers ask about your strengths and weaknesses. For example, they might ask, 'Tell me about a time you solved a problem.' You should prepare some stories about your projects.
Okay, I will try to prepare. By the way, do you think I should wear a suit or something casual? I guess I don't want to look too formal.

Actually, it depends on the company. In big cities like Beijing, people often wear suits. But in Wuhan, many tech companies prefer smart casual clothes. You can wear a nice shirt and trousers, but no tie, I think.
Great advice. I am drinking a cup of jasmine tea now. It tastes good. Do you have any tips for the salary negotiation part?

Well, you should research the market first. In Hubei, the average salary for a librarian is around 4,000 to 5,000 yuan. You can say, 'I am interested in this role, but I hope the salary fits my experience.' Don't be too aggressive, though.
I understand. Maybe I can also ask about the training program. What if they reject offer less money but better training?

That is a good point. In addition to money, benefits like overtime pay and holidays are important. For example, if they offer a flexible schedule, it might be worth less cash. You have to decide what you value most.
You are right. My career goal is to manage a team in three years. Does that change how I should answer questions?

Absolutely. You can mention your ambition in your cover letter. Say something like, 'I hope to grow into a team leader role in the future.' It shows you are serious and motivated. Good luck with your interview next week!

messages.content: Hi Fang, I am planning to take the high-speed train from Nanning to my grandparents home in Wuzhou this weekend. Do you think I need to book the ticket since last month?

Well, yes, you should book it in advance. Actually, trains on weekends are very busy, and you have to book since three months ago if you want a seat with a window. I booked my ticket for the Guangzhou trip last week because it was full.
Oh, I see. I want a seat with a view of the hills. Where should I go to find the right platform at the station in the morning?

You know, the best way is to look at the big screen in the main hall. It shows the train number and the platform, so you do not need to ask anyone. By the way, the station near the Qingxiu Mountain neighborhood is very big, so arrive one hour before your train leaves.
That is good advice. I am worried about getting lost in the station. If I miss the platform, can I still catch the train?

To be honest, it is risky if you miss the platform, because the train will not wait for you. Actually, you should check the announcement again when you are in the waiting area. If you are late, you might need to take the next train, which is usually later.
I guess I will arrive early then. What kind of food is good to eat on the high-speed train? Do you like the meals they sell?

Well, the food on the train is okay, but it is a bit expensive. I usually buy fresh dumplings or noodles from a small shop before I get on. For example, you can try the rice noodles from Nanning, which taste really good and are not too hot.
Dumplings sound delicious! I have not tried the local rice noodles yet. Can I bring my own food, like a fruit cake or some milk tea?

Of course, you can bring your own food. Actually, many people bring snacks like fruit cake or a thermos of milk tea to save money. Just make sure you have a small bag so you do not block the aisle with your things.
I will bring a bottle of milk tea from the local brand. Thanks for your help, Fang. I hope the trip is smooth.
You are welcome. I think you will enjoy the trip because the scenery is beautiful in the spring. Have a safe journey to your grandparents, and call me when you get there so I know you are safe.
I will call you. I am sure I will see the mountains. See you next week!

messages.content: Hi Fang. I want to take the high-speed train to Guilin this weekend. It's spring now, so the weather must be nice. But I don't know how to book the ticket yet. Can you help me?

Hello, Wei Ming. Actually, you can book tickets online on the China Railway website or use the App since they are very convenient. However, you need to book in advance because the trains to Guilin are popular in spring. You should check the schedule today.
Oh, I see. I will check the website right now. But I am worried about the price. Is it expensive compared to flying? Also, do I need to print the ticket?

Well, it depends on how early you book. If you book a week ago, it's usually cheaper than flying. By the way, you do not need to print the ticket anymore. You can just show the QR code on your phone at the station.
That is great news. I like my phone. But where should I go at the Nanning station to find my platform? Is it easy to get there from the Qingxiu Mountain neighborhood?

Yes, it's quite close to the Qingxiu Mountain area, so you can walk or take a taxi easily. Inside the station, follow the signs that say "High-Speed Speed Speed speed train" because the gates are separate. Actually, the staff is very helpful if you get lost.
Good. I hope I don't miss the gate. When we are on the train, can we eat? I want to bring some rice noodles from home, but maybe I should buy food on the train instead?

Honesty, you can bring your own food, but the train staff sells snacks and drinks too. For example, they have fresh dumplings and bubble tea which are delicious. If you want something warm, buying it on the train might be better because the train is moving.
Bubble dumplings sound nice! I haven't tried them on a train before. What if the train is full of people? Will it be comfortable for me to sleep?

Well, high-speed trains have two classes: second class and first class. Second class is like a bus, so it can be crowded in the morning. But first class is more comfortable if you want to rest. In addition, the seats are reclining and there is air conditioning.
I think first class is better for me. I have a lot of homework next week, so I want to relax. But I am not sure if I can afford it. Do you know if the price difference is big?

To be honest, the price is higher, but it's not too expensive. You pay about twice as much as second class. Actually, if you book early, sometimes there are discounts for students like you. It's worth it if you need a good sleep.
Okay, I will try to book first class. Thank you for your advice, Fang. I feel much more confident now. Do you think I should bring some books to read during the trip?

Yes, that's a great idea! The journey takes about three hours, so you have enough time. However, make sure the Wi-Fi works on the train because sometimes it is slow. Well, enjoy your trip to Guilin and see your grandparents soon!

messages.content: Hi Zhang Wei! I'm Jing Ya, and I'm looking for some souvenirs to give to my friends back in Beijing. The weather here in Dali is so hot right now, perfect for walking around.

Hello Jing Ya! It's a pleasure to meet you. Well, you're very lucky because the afternoon sun makes the colors of the local crafts really pop. I sell many traditional items here in the ancient town that would look great in Beijing.
That sounds amazing. I've been walking around for an hour, but I haven't found anything special yet. Do you have any recommendations for something I can buy easily?

Actually, a hand-carved bamboo birdcage is a great choice. It's a classic from this area, and your friends will love it. I've sold quite a few of them since last summer. By the way, bamboo is very durable, so it won't break easily.
Oh, a bamboo birdcage? That's very unique. But I'm not sure if my friends like birds. Maybe something with local food is better. What about some tea?

Good idea! You know, our local tea is famous for being fresh and sweet. I have some Pu'er tea cakes that are wrapped in special paper. If you buy them, I can wrap them in nice red paper for you to give as a gift.
That sounds perfect. How much does one cake cost? I remember prices in Beijing are usually higher, so I hope this is affordable.

To be honest, it depends on the quality. A standard one is about fifty yuan, but the older ones can be two hundred. You can bargain with me, but don't make the price too low or I will feel sad. For example, if you say one hundred, I might think you are jokingestingying.
Oh, I see. So I should start with a lower number? I guess I will try to talk to you nicely. Can I take a few pieces if I buy the red wrapping paper too?

Yes, that's a good way to bargain! You can ask for three pieces for two hundred yuan. It's not a big deal for me if you buy the wrapping paper too. I've had many customers from the north ask for this before.
Okay, let's say I want three pieces. But wait, how do I wrap them properly? I don't want to ruin the presentation when I give them to my friends next week.

Don't worry! I can wrap them for you right now. I will use a red cloth and tie it with a blue string, which is very traditional. Actually, the red color brings good luck, so your friends will feel happy when they open the box.
That is very thoughtful of you. Thank you for helping me choose. I think I will buy the three pieces and let you wrap them. It's been a long walk, but this feels worth it.
You are welcome! I think you made a good decision. Now, let's go to the counter so I can count the money and pack everything. Hope you enjoy your trip back to Beijing!

messages.content: Hi! I'm Jing Ya. I've been walking around the old town since morning, and I really like the atmosphere here. By the way, do you sell traditional souvenirs?

Hello, Jing Ya! Yes, of course we do. Well, this market is famous for handmade things like Dongba paintings and silver bracelets. Actually, many tourists buy these to send to their friends in Beijing or Shanghai.
That sounds interesting. I have a few friends back in the capital who love culture. Are the paintings too expensive? I'm on a budget, you know.

They can be a bit pricey if you choose the best quality. For example, a small one might cost 300 yuan, but a large one could be 1,000 yuan. To be honest, you can find cheaper ones if you look carefully at the stalls near the main street.
I see. Maybe I'll start with a smaller one. Do you know how I can bargain? I usually don't know how to negotiate prices in Chinese markets.

Oh, that is normal! Well, you can just say the price is a little too high and ask for a discount. For instance, if the seller says 500 yuan, you can try offering 350 yuan. Although they might not agree at first, it is often worth trying.
That's a good tip. By the way, if I buy something, how should I wrap it properly for travel? I don't want to break it on the bus.

You should ask the shop owner to wrap it for you. They usually use strong paper and tie it with red string, which is very traditional. Actually, for fragile items like pottery, they might put bubble wrap inside first. It's safer than carrying it in a regular plastic bag.
Perfect. I also want to buy some local snacks, like the famous rice paper rolls. Do you think they taste as good as they look?

Yes, they are delicious! Well, the taste depends on the filling. If you choose the ones with fresh meat or vegetables, they are very tasty. In addition, the rice paper is thin and soft, so it is easy to eat. Many people prefer them because they are healthy.
I agree. Actually, I've tried them before in Chengdu, but these here seem even better. How much would a box of ten rolls cost?

A box of ten usually costs around 20 yuan. However, if you buy more than two boxes, the price might go down a bit. You can also ask if there are any special offers during the summer holiday season. It's a good time to visit, you know.
That sounds reasonable. I think I'll buy one box of rolls and a small painting. Do you have any specific brands you recommend?

Well, we don't use big brands here; everything is handmade by local artists. I suggest you check the signature on the painting. For example, a piece signed by a master artist is better, but it also costs more. Anyway, I can help you pick one if you like.
Great, thank you! I'll let you help me. One last question, can I pay with my phone? I don't have enough cash on me right now.

messages.content: Hi Ma Lin. I've been wanting to learn calligraphy since I came back to Guangzhou, but I don't know where to start.

That's great, Sun Lei! Well, actually, it's never too late to pick up a traditional skill. In the Xiguan neighborhood, we have a very nice studio with good brushes and special Xuan paper. You should try it here first.
Oh, I've heard of Xuan paper. But I am worried about the ink. Is it hard to buy?

Don't worry, it's easy. We use real soybean ink, which is very smooth. If you buy a good bottle, it lasts a long time. Although it costs a bit more than Western ink, it's worth it for the smell and the color.
Yes, I think so. The smell of the ink reminds me of my grandfather's home in Chengdu. He used to write poems all the time.
That's beautiful. Connecting with your family history is a very important reason to learn this. By the way, do you have any specific style you want to practice, like Kai or Running script?
I guess I want to start with Running script. It looks more fluid than the standard one.

Running script is a great choice for beginners who want to express themselves. It's faster than Regular script, but still has structure. We have some examples from the Tang Dynasty that you can look at.
Can I bring my own paper? I bought some nice rice paper in Beijing.

You can try it, but I think the paper from the local shop might work better with our ink. Rice paper is a bit too thin sometimes. If you use the thick Xuan paper, the ink won't bleed through the fibers.
Oh, I see. I will buy some new paper next week. Do you display the artwork in the studio?
Yes, we have a small wall for students to show their work. It's a fun way to see how others improve over time. To be honest, seeing your first piece on that wall would make me very proud.
That sounds wonderful. I want to show my family when I come back from work.
That's a wonderful idea. Your family will love seeing you connect with your roots again. We can schedule a class for this Saturday if you like. Just let me know!

messages.content: Hello, Ma Lin. I am Sun Lei. I have been practicing calligraphy for a long time, but my hand still shakes. What should I do?
Hello, Sun Lei. Well, it is very common for beginners to shake at first. I have seen many students like you. You know, if you practice every day for only ten minutes, your hand will get stronger.
That is good advice. But the ink is too wet today. The paper absorbs it too fast. Do you have special paper for this?
Actually, you should use Xuan paper, which is special for ink. It holds the brush well. By the way, do you use real ink sticks or the bottled ink? Bott the bottled kind is easier for beginners.
I use the bottled ink because it is convenient. However, I want to try real ink sticks. Can I use them in this small room?
Of course you can! The smell is wonderful. To be honest, grinding the ink stick yourself makes the painting better. You have to add a little water slowly. It takes patience, but it is worth it.
I agree. I think I will buy some real ink next week. Where should I buy it in Guangzhou? I live in Tianhe District.
You can go to a traditional shop near Tianhe, or maybe visit a market in Liwan District. There are many old shops there. For example, you can find high-quality ink there.
Liwan sounds interesting. But I am busy with work on weekdays. Can I go on the weekend?
Yes, the weekend is perfect. Also, you can join our class on Saturday morning. We meet at the cultural center near the metro station. It is very convenient.
That would be great. After I finish the painting, where can I display it? Do you have a wall at the center?
Well, we have a small corner for students' work. You can hang it there. Actually, many people come to see the art during the holiday. It is a good way to show your progress.
I am excited about that. Maybe I will write a poem for the New Year next time. Thank you for your help.
You are welcome. Writing a Spring Festival couplet is a great tradition. I think you will improve quickly if you keep practicing. See you next Saturday!

messages.content: Hi! I am Xiao Ya. I want to help our neighborhood with the spring festival. Have you joined the event committee yet?
Hello, Xiao Ya! Yes, I have joined since last month. Actually, I am working at the community center here in Dali. It's been busy since the snow melted.
Wow, Dali is so beautiful. I think we need more volunteers because many people are busy with their exams. Do you know how to recruit recruit more helpers?
Well, you can post notices in the school hallway. You know, many students have free time after school. I have also told my friends who live in the old neighborhood near Erhai Lake.
That is a good idea. What about the budget? I don't have enough money to buy decorations. Can we use money from the community fund?
Of course, the community fund has enough money. However, we still need to plan carefully. For example, red lanterns are expensive, but we can borrow them from the temple on Qingyan Street.
Oh, I didn't know that. What if it rains on the day of the festival? It will be hard to hang the decorations.
You are right. If it rains, we can move the lanterns to the covered pavilion. Anyway, we should prepare umbrellas for the guests who come to eat fried noodles.
Good point. When should we start making the plan? I guess we can start this Saturday if we finish our homework.
I think Saturday is perfect! Actually, I will meet you there at 2 pm. We can also discuss who will cook the mooncakes for the celebration.
Yes, let's do it. Do you think it is important to invite people from other villages too? We want everyone to be happy.
Absolutely! If we invite neighbors from Sanlang Village, the festival will be much more lively. You know, their drum team is very famous.
That sounds exciting. I will tell the teachers at my school. They might help us with the music.
Great! Since you have offered to help, the committee will be very happy. See you this Saturday, Xiao Ya!

Hi Xiao Ya! Well, that's great. Actually, we're looking for people to join the event committee right now. You know, it's going to be very busy this year.
Oh, I'm interested. Have you done the planning before?
Yes, I've helped organize it for three years since I started working at the community center. To be honest, it's challenging, but it's also very rewarding.
What are the main things we need to do?
Well, the most important part is recruiting more volunteers, because we only have a few people so far. In addition, we need to plan the decoration schedule for the square.
I guess I can help with decorations. Do you like red paper cuttings?
Of course! Red paper cuttings are traditional and they look beautiful. Actually, if you have some experience, that would be perfect for the main stage.
My mom makes them. But I'm worried about the budget.
That's a good point. We've spent quite a bit of money on food for the volunteers already. However, we can save money on decorations if we use local materials.
That makes sense. When is the festival happening again?
It's on the 15th of the first lunar lunar lunar lunar, which is next Saturday. So, we have two weeks to finish everything. If we work hard now, it will be ready.
I'll sign up today. Can we meet at the center at 4 PM?
Sure, that works perfectly. See you then! Actually, please bring your drawing tools if you can.

messages.content: Hi, I need to buy some fresh pork for the dumplings at the market near my home in Hangzhou.
I think that's a great idea. Well, the market on Hefang Street is usually very busy before the holiday, but the meat there is really fresh.

Okay, I will buy those. But now I am worried about the seating. Should we put the elders in the main seat?
Of course! You know, in China, the elders always sit in the place of honor. We must respect them.
Right. My grandfather said he used to sit there every year since he was young. It is a very important tradition.
Yes, I think that's because it shows our gratitude. Although I was born in Beijing, I remember my family did the same thing.
That is nice. By the way, can you help me carry the heavy table to the living room? I am not strong enough today.
No problem. I'll help you move it. In addition, let's set the table first so everything is ready when the guests arrive.
Good idea. If we finish now, we can cook together. I guess the kitchen will be very crowded.
It will be, but that's normal. To be honest, cooking together is the best part of the reunion dinner.
I agree. Let's start with the rice. My uncle will come from Ningbo tomorrow, so we need to prepare everything.
Yes, let's make sure the rice cooker is ready. I hope he has a safe trip since the weather might be rainy.

messages.content: Hi, my name is Liu Xia. I am a new employee here. I have been working in a university library since last month, but I have never worked in a shop before. I am a bit nervous.

Hello, Xia! Well, don't worry, actually. I think you will do great. You know, working in a bookstore is very different from a library, but your experience will help. By the way, have you seen the new uniform yet?
Yes, I saw it this morning. It is a dark blue jacket and a skirt pair of black trousers. It looks nice, but I think it is a bit hot. Do I need to wear it today?

Of course, you need to wear it today. It's the policy, and it helps customers recognize the staff. Actually, the fabric is cotton, so it's not that hot even if it's sunny outside. If you feel too warm, you can just take off the jacket later in the day.
Okay, I will wear it. Thank you. Now, how do I handle the books? The shelves are very high. I have been organizing books at home, but the system here is different. Is it difficult?

It's not difficult at all, I promise. You know, we use a special card system here. For example, if a book is about history, you put it in the section with that color tag. Actually, I can show you how to use the ladder. It's quite high, but it's safe if you hold the rail.
That sounds easy. I can do it. But what if a customer is angry? I read a book about customer service, but I am not sure how to deal with difficult people. Maybe they will complain about the price.

Oh, don't worry about that. To be honest, most customers are very kind here. However, if someone is unhappy, you just need to listen to them and apologize. For example, you can say, 'I'm sorry, I understand your point.' Usually, they will calm down after that. It's simple once you try it.
I understand. I will try to listen. What about the schedule? I have been working eight hours a day at my old job, but this place seems to have many shifts. Do I have to work on weekends?

Well, actually, our hours are a bit flexible. You don't have to work every weekend, but we need someone here for the busy times. For example, Saturday morning is very crowded because many students come to study. If you can work one Saturday a month, that would be perfect. What do you think?
I can work on Saturdays. I am free this Saturday morning. But I am worried I will make a mistake. I have never sold a book before. Is it expensive to buy books here?

It's very reasonable, I think. The prices are lower than other shops in the city. By the way, we have some special books on sale this week. If you help sell them, you can get a small bonus. Actually, I'm sure you will do well, since you are so careful.

That is good news. I am happy to get a bonus. One more thing, can I take a break to drink tea? I feel thirsty because the shop is very quiet and I have been standing for a long time. Is there a place to sit?

Yes, of course! You can take a short break every hour. There's a small room in the back where you can sit and drink tea. Actually, I often have a cup of green tea there to relax. You should rest now since it's been a while since you started.
Thank you so much, Manager. I will rest now. I feel much better. I think I am ready to start my shift again. Maybe I can help a customer with a textbook.
That's a great idea, Xia. You're doing well already! Well, go ahead and greet the customers. If you need any help, just call me. I think you'll love working here soon.

messages.content: Hi Manager, I'm Liu Xia. I just finished my degree at Shaanxi Normal University and I'm really nervous about starting this new part-time job in your bookstore on East Baqi Road.

Hello Liu Xia! Well, don't worry, you're going to be just fine. Actually, I've hired many fresh graduates since I started managing here last year. It's completely normal to feel a bit anxious when you first walk into a new workplace.
That's true. The uniform looks strange, though. It's a dark blue jacket with a big logo on the chest. Do I need to iron it before I come to work tomorrow?

Oh, you've got good eyes! Yes, please iron the jacket, but be careful not to burn the fabric. Actually, our laundry room has some special hangers that keep the shoulders looking nice. By the way, have you tried the steamed buns at the shop next door? They're delicious if you want a quick lunch.
I have not eaten lunch yet. I will buy a steamed bun. But what about the customers? I heard they can be very difficult sometimes. Last week, a man shouted at a worker in a coffee shop in Beijing.

Ah, dealing with difficult customers is always a challenge. Honestly, it depends on the situation. If a customer is shouting, you should stay calm and listen to them politely. For example, if someone complains about a book, you can say, 'I understand your concern, and I will check for you.' You'll get used to it after a few weeks.
I guess I will try that. What about the schedule? I need to go back to my dorm in Beilin District at 5 PM. Is it possible to work only until 4:30 PM on Fridays?

That's a reasonable request, but our Friday shifts are usually full until 6 PM because many students come back from the library then. Well, let me check the roster. Actually, we have a flexible system if you finish your reading tasks early. You could finish your shift one hour early if you help organize the shelves first.
Oh, that sounds helpful. I think I can organize the shelves quickly. My sister works in a shop in Xi'an and she says the shelves get messy very fast.

Yes, that makes sense. My sister also works in retail, and she always says organization is key to a smooth day. To be honest, I'd be happy to have someone who knows how to tidy up efficiently. We can start with the fiction section tomorrow morning. What time do you usually leave your university?
I usually leave at 11 AM on weekdays, but sometimes I stay until 1 PM if I have a big exam. Do I need to bring my own lunch? I like hot pot, but I don't know if you have a break room.

You don't need to bring your own lunch; the cafeteria in the back of the store sells cheap noodles and rice for staff. Although hot pot is great, it's a bit too heavy for a quick lunch break. By the way, since you're new, I've already booked a seat in the four-bed compartment at the staff dormitory near the subway station for you tonight.
Wow, thank you so much! I have never lived in a staff dormitory before. Is it quiet? I need to study for my English test.

It's quite quiet during the evening, especially after 9 PM. Actually, most staff members use the time to study or rest. You know, the subway line 2 is very convenient, so you can get there in about ten minutes from your university. I'll walk you there tomorrow.
That is wonderful. I feel much better now. I hope I don't make any mistakes in the first few days.

You won't make any serious mistakes, I promise. In fact, I've seen you make progress since we started talking. Take your time, and remember that learning the store procedures takes practice. Just ask me if you have any questions about the schedule or the customers. Have a great day, Liu Xia!

messages.content: Hi! I'm Wei. I'm thinking of taking the high-speed train to Yunnan next month. Have you ever traveled there?
Hello, Wei! Yes, I actually just took the train from Changsha to Kunming last week. It was amazing! The speed is very fast.
That sounds great. How do I book the ticket? I know I can use an app, but is it easy?
Well, it's quite easy! You can use apps like 12306 or travel apps. You just need to enter your name and ID number. I booked my ticket since last month because I wanted to get a good seat.
Oh, I see. Do I need to print the ticket or can I show my phone screen at the station?
You don't need to print it anymore. You can just show the QR code on your phone. Actually, many people do it that way now. It saves time at the gate.
Good. I have a lot of luggage. My suitcase is heavy. Is it allowed on the train?
Yes, of course! You can put your suitcase on the overhead rack. But if you have very heavy bags, it might be hard to lift them. I usually pack light for the trip.
That's a good idea. Will the train stop in small towns along the way? I want to see some places before Kunming.
It depends on the route. The high-speed line doesn't stop at every small town, but you can change trains at bigger cities. For example, you could stop in Liuyang or Changde to see the scenery.
Liuyang sounds nice. What should I eat there? I like Chinese food.
There are many good places to eat! You can try some local Hunan snacks like spicy rice noodles or dumplings. By the way, did you know there are also nice tea houses in the smaller towns?
Tea sounds perfect for a rainy afternoon. I guess I will try to stop there if I have time.
That's a great plan! Enjoy your trip to Yunnan. The scenery there is really beautiful. I think you will love it!
Thank you! I hope the weather is good when I arrive.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Wei. I'm thinking of taking the high-speed train to Dali next month. Have you ever traveled there?
Yes, I actually just came back from Kunming to Changsha. I took the train from Changsha to Kunming, and then I changed trains to go to Dali. It was really convenient!
That sounds great. Did you book your tickets online? I heard it's hard to get seats if you wait until the last minute.
Well, yes, I booked everything on my phone before the holiday. You know, it's much faster than going to the station window. If I had waited, I probably wouldn't have gotten a seat in first class.
I see. I've been trying to buy a ticket, but the website is slow. Also, I have a lot of luggage. Do I need to take it onto the train?

To be honest, you definitely need to take your luggage on the train. Unlike some other countries, you can't leave your suitcases in the station. I put my big bag in the overhead rack, and my small one under my seat.
Oh, I guess I'll have to pack lightly. So, how long does the trip take from Changsha to Kunming? Is it comfortable for sleeping?

It takes about twelve hours. The seats are comfortable, but it's not an overnight sleeper train. You can bring a blanket though. By the way, I bought some local snacks at the station to eat during the journey.
What snacks did you buy? Do you have any recommendations for food in Dali?
I ate some rice noodles and hot pot when I got there. Actually, the food in Dali is amazing. You should try the roasted fish and some fresh fruit. The weather is also very nice there in autumn.
That sounds delicious. I'm planning to stop in a small town near Dali, maybe Xizhou. Is it easy to get there from the main station?
Yes, it's quite easy. You can take a local bus or a taxi from Dali Station to Xizhou. It only takes about twenty minutes. I took a bus, and it was cheap and not too crowded.
That's perfect. I think I'll do the same. Thank you for your advice. I hope the train runs on time.

Don't worry, the high-speed rail is usually very reliable. I've taken it many times, and delays are rare. Just make sure you check the schedule on your phone the day before you travel. Enjoy your trip!

messages.content: Hi! I'm Lin. I've been looking for some traditional gifts to send home since yesterday. Do you have any good recommendations here in Chengdu?

Hello, Lin! Well, yes, we have many great things here. Actually, if you want something spicy and famous, you should try the hotpot base or some Sichuan peppercorns. By the way, are you looking for food items or maybe something for tea lovers?
That sounds interesting. I love tea, so I might buy some tea leaves. But I also heard that the snacks in the old street are very popular. Can you tell me about the snacks?

Oh, absolutely! To be honest, the snacks are amazing. For example, we have spicy dried beef and roasted sweet potatoes. The dried beef is usually very tender and has a nice numbing taste because of the Sichuan pepper. Have you ever eaten it before?
No, I haven't tried it yet. Is it very spicy? I am worried about my family's stomach. They are not used to such strong flavors.

I see. Well, it can be quite spicy, but we also have a mild version if you ask. Actually, you know, you can mix it with some sugar or less pepper. If I were your family, I would start with a little bit just to test it. Do you think they would like that?
That is a good idea. I think I will buy the mild one. How much is it? I want to make sure the price is not too high.

It's quite reasonable, I guess. A small packet costs about twenty yuan, and a big one is around forty yuan. In addition, we have tea sets which are also very popular as gifts. They are usually made of porcelain and look very nice. Would you like to see some?
Yes, please show me the tea sets. I have been collecting them since I was a child. But I need to compare the prices with the market in Wuhou District first.

Of course! We are right here in the Wuhou District, so the prices should be fair. Actually, you know, many people come here from other cities to buy these sets. For example, this one has blue flowers on it and costs only fifty yuan. Is that within your budget?
Fifty yuan is perfect. I think I will buy one tea set and the mild spicy beef. But wait, do you have any other places nearby where I can compare the prices?

Yes, there is another market just across the street called Jintai. It's quite busy, especially on weekends. However, I think our prices are a bit better because we sell fresh goods daily. If you go there, you might find similar things, but honestly, ours are fresher. What do you think?
I agree. I will buy here then. Thank you so much for your help. I have never been to such a busy market before, and I really enjoyed looking at all these items.
You are very welcome, Lin! I'm glad you liked it. Well, here is your tea set and the spicy beef. I hope your family loves them. Please come back again if you need anything else. Have a nice day!

messages.content: Hi! I'm Lin. I'm looking for some traditional gifts to send to my family in Beijing. Do you have any spicy snacks here?
Hello Lin! Yes, I think you'll find some great things here. Well, we sell famous spicy snacks like la zha jiang and dried beef from Jiuzhaigou. They are very popular with tourists.
That sounds interesting. Have you tried the la zha jiang yourself? Is it too hot for me?

I've tried it many times since I opened this shop last year. To be honest, it can be quite hot, but you can ask for less chili if you want. Actually, many people buy it for the flavor, not just the heat.
I guess I should be careful then. What about prices? Are they expensive compared to buying online?

That's a good question. Prices here might be a bit higher than online because you are buying fresh goods. However, you get quality assurance products that you can't find on the internet. For example, this dried duck is made right now in our kitchen.
I see. I've been shopping in Wuhou District for a while now. The market is very busy today because it is Sunday morning.
Yes, I'm sure it is! The sun is shining and many people are looking for souvenirs. You know, this is the best time to visit. If you wait until tomorrow, everything will be closed.
Right, I don't want to miss out. Can I also buy some tea? My family loves Chinese tea.
Of course! We have excellent Pu'er tea from Yunnan Province. It has been aged for many years, so the taste is very smooth. In addition, we sell green tea from Longjing in Hangzhou too.
Wow, that sounds delicious. Do you think the tea is worth the money? I am worried about the cost.
I think it is worth it. Although the price is high, the tea is very good for your health. You can brew a pot and share it with your friends. It's a nice tradition in China.
That makes sense. I'll take the spicy beef and the Pu'er tea. How much is everything with the tax?
Sure, let me check. The total is 250 yuan, which includes tax. Here is the receipt. I hope you enjoy the food and the tea when you get home!
Thank you so much! I will definitely try the beef. See you next time.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Jing. I've been painting outside Xixi Wetland since morning, and now I'm thinking about hiking this weekend. Do you like going into nature?
Hello Jing! Yes, I love it. Actually, I've been hiking near Xixi for a few years because the air is so fresh. Did you know that the trails around the wetland are perfect in spring?
That sounds great. But I'm worried about the weather. It rained a lot last week. What is the forecast for Saturday?

Well, I checked the app this morning. It says it will be sunny and warm, although there might be a little breeze. If it rains, the ground will be muddy, but I think Saturday will be clear. Have you packed your clothes yet?
I bought some new hiking boots last month, but I haven't checked my bag. Should I bring a heavy jacket or just a light one?
To be honest, you don't need a heavy coat if the sun is out. Just bring a light windbreaker because it can get a bit chilly in the afternoon shade. By the way, did you pack any water bottles?
Yes, I have two bottles. I usually drink tea after hiking, but can I bring hot tea from a thermos?
Of course! Hot jasmine tea is a great idea. You know, many hikers stop at the small tea house near the bridge to drink it. It helps you relax after a long walk. Have you decided which trail to take?
I'm not sure. I heard there is a path near the West Lake, but I don't know the way. Is it hard?

Actually, that path is very beautiful but a bit long. If you go early, you can see the willow trees clearly. However, if you want something shorter, try the trail near the Plum Bloss Bloss Garden. It's easier for beginners.
I think I will go to the Plum Garden. My friend told me the flowers are very pretty this time of year. When should we meet?
That sounds like a perfect plan! We should meet at the main gate at 9 AM so we don't get late. I'll bring some dumplings and noodles for lunch. Would you like to try them?
Yes, dumplings sound delicious. I haven't eaten them in weeks. Let's meet then. Thank you for helping me plan my trip!
You're welcome! I've been looking forward to this. We will have a great time, and I think you'll love the view over the water. See you on Saturday!

messages.content: Hi Lin, I'm thinking of going hiking this weekend. I love nature, but I haven't been in the mountains since last autumn.
Hi Jing! That's a great idea. Actually, the weather in Hangzhou has been perfect lately. It's not too hot and the air is fresh. Have you checked the forecast for Saturday yet?
Oh, I see. I looked at it this morning. It says there will be a little rain in the afternoon, but the morning looks sunny.
Well, that's actually okay. We can start early! By the way, do you want to meet near Xixi Wetland first? There is a small trail there that is very beautiful this time of year.
Yes, I've heard about Xixi Wetland. But is it hard to walk? I usually wear my comfortable shoes, but I'm not sure if I have the right clothes.
To be honest, it's not too difficult. The path is flat mostly, although there are some muddy spots near the water. You should wear a light jacket because it might get cool when the rain starts.
Good point. I'll bring a jacket. What else should I pack? Do you need a big backpack or something smaller?
A medium-sized bag would be perfect. You know, you can carry a bottle of water and some snacks like dumplings or rice cakes. Also, don't forget your camera! The scenery is amazing.
I definitely need my camera. I haven't taken any photos of nature since I moved to this city. Oh, and where exactly are we going on the trail?
We can start at the north gate and walk along the West Lake side. It's quite famous because many artists like you go there to paint or take pictures.
That sounds wonderful. I'll pack my bag tonight. Do you think we should rent a bike to go back or walk the whole way?
I guess walking the whole way is better for your exercise. But if you are tired, we can rent a bicycle near the gate on the way back. What do you think?
Walking sounds better for me. I want to enjoy the view. Thanks for the advice, Lin. I'm really looking forward to this trip!
You're welcome! I'm sure you'll have a great time. We will meet at the gate at 8 AM, right? See you then!

messages.content: Hi Li Wei. I've been thinking about joining a volunteer group near West Lake, but I don't know where to start.

Hey Yi! Well, actually there are a few groups that meet on weekends. For example, the Green Lake Volunteers have been cleaning up the park since last spring. They usually gather at 9 a.m. on Saturdays.
That sounds good. However, I'm a bit worried about the schedule because I have to study for my exams next month.

I think you can still do it if you check the calendar first. They sometimes move the activity to Sunday afternoon if many students have classes. Also, you know, it's not every week, so you won't miss too much study time.
Oh, that's helpful. Do you think I should organize a small group with my classmates instead? Maybe we can just pick a day.

That's a great idea! In fact, many students in our university organize their own clean-ups near the library or the old street. If you invite three or four friends, it's easier to agree on a time, like next Sunday morning.
I guess I should send WeChat messages to them soon. What kind of things do they usually collect?

Well, they mostly pick up plastic bottles, cigarette butts, and old newspapers. Sometimes there are also fallen leaves in the autumn, but now in spring, the main problem is trash from picnickers near the lake shore.
Actually, I heard that some people leave food wrappers. Do you think we should take bags to carry them?

Of course! You must take thick plastic bags because the trash can be wet. We also need gloves, which are cheap at the supermarket. By the way, don't forget to bring water, although it's spring, it can still be a bit cool in the morning.
Got it. If we organize it, should we tell the park management office beforehand?

Yes, you should call them. It shows you are serious and they might even give you some tools. I remember last year a group did that, and the manager was very happy to see students helping. He even brought us some lemon tea after the work!
That would be amazing. I'll try to contact the office this weekend. Thanks for the advice, Li Wei!
You're welcome! I guess we can meet at the bus stop near Huajiadu Road on Saturday to plan the details. Let's make it happen, Yi!

messages.content: Hi, I'm Yi. I've been thinking about joining a community cleanup group here in Hangzhou. Have you done something like this before?

Hi Yi! Well, yes, I have organized a few cleanups since last spring. Actually, we usually meet near West Lake on Saturday mornings. It's a lot of fun because the weather is nice, and we help the park look better.
That sounds great. To be honest, I haven't joined any volunteer group yet. When exactly do you schedule these activities?
We usually pick the weekend after the Chinese New Year, or sometimes in May. For example, if it rains on Saturday, we might move to Sunday. Do you prefer mornings or afternoons?
I guess mornings are better for me. I've been studying hard for my exams, but I need a break. Would you like to organize a group with my classmates?

That would be perfect! I think it's a good idea to bring more people. Actually, we can start with just your class. If we recruit together, it will be easier to clean the garbage near the Longjing tea plantations.
I've never cleaned near the tea fields, but I'd like to try. What should we take with us? Do we need special tools?
Well, you just need gloves and trash bags. By the way, we usually bring some water and fruit, like apples or oranges, to eat after the work. It's important to stay hydrated in the spring sun.
Oh, I forgot about the fruit! That's a good idea. Can we buy the fruit at a nearby store?
Of course. There's a small market just across the street from the entrance. You can also grab some hot tea from a vendor there if you want. It's a bit expensive, but the quality is very good.
I see. So, if I tell my classmates about this, can we join your next event this coming Saturday?
Yes, that works. Actually, we haven't finalized the time yet because some people can't come. I'll send you a message later to confirm the details. What's your phone number?
My number is 138-xxxx-1234. Thank you for helping me plan this. I'm really looking forward to it.
You're welcome! It's great that you want to help the neighborhood. I'll call you tomorrow to check if everyone is ready. See you soon!

messages.content: Hi Lao Zhang, I'm actually here because I run a small gift shop in Kunming. I need some high-quality loose leaf tea to stock up for spring sales.

Oh, that's great to hear! Well, I'm very happy to help you since my shop has been supplying gift shops all over the south for years. What kind of tea are you looking for? For example, do you prefer the delicate Longjing or something stronger like Ke Pu'er?
Actually, I think Longjing is a must-have for my customers who love Hangzhou. But to be honest, I'm worried about the price. Do you offer wholesale rates if I buy in bulk?

That's true, the price can be a bit high if you buy just a little bit. However, if you order at least five kilograms, I can give you a much better deal. You know, many people buy from me because they trust my quality, so I'm not afraid to negotiate.
That sounds promising. In addition to the price, how do you ensure the tea is fresh? My customers have complained before that some tea smells like old dust.

I completely understand your concern. Actually, I've been roasting the tea myself every morning since last winter to keep it fresh. The ones in the back are from this year, while the older ones are dried carefully. If you take a sample home, you can smell the difference right away.
I'd love to try a sample. Also, could you help me with the packaging? My clients expect the tea to come in nice ceramic jars with a traditional seal.

Of course, that's a good idea for presenting the gift. I can use the blue ceramic jars which are very popular in Hangzhou, and I'll put a red wax seal on them. It takes a bit more time, but it's worth it if you want to impress your buyers.
Perfect. One last thing, if I order today, can you have it shipped to my shop in Kunming before the May 1st holiday rush?

That should be no problem. Although the spring season is busy, I usually ship the bulk orders by train within two days. So, if we finish today, the tea will be on the road before the holiday starts. Does that work for your schedule?

messages.content: Hey, have you tried the food stalls here by the Yulong River yet? I'm actually looking for a place that serves very spicy snacks, not just normal meals. I want to test my tolerance!

Oh, well, that's a great idea! To be honest, the spicy oil noodles here are famous, although they might be too hot for some people. I've been eating at the stall near the Xijiang Bridge since last year, and the owner adds extra chili oil if you ask.
Wow, sounds intense! But do they have any dishes that are spicy but still have some meat in them? I'm getting a bit hungry.

Actually, yes! You can try the spicy beef skewers or the stir-fried pork with garlic. They're really tasty. In fact, I remember last time I ate the pork, and it was so good because the sauce is very flavorful.
That sounds perfect. How much are the skewers usually? I don't want to spend too much money tonight.

Well, it's very affordable! Each skewer is only about ten yuan, so you can buy many without worrying about the price. Compared to the big restaurants in the city center, the prices here are much lower since last summer.
Perfect. Do you think I should bring some water with me, or is there a place nearby to buy drinks?

I guess you should bring a bottle just in case. There's a small shop selling local rice tea and lemonade nearby, which helps cool down your mouth. You know, the lemonade is really refreshing if you drink it after eating spicy food.
Great, thanks! One more thing, have you noticed any new stalls opening here recently?

Oh, yes! A new stall selling fried tofu and sweet potato chips opened last week. It's near the entrance of the night market. Although I haven't tried it yet, everyone says the tofu is crispy and delicious.
That sounds interesting. Maybe I'll try the tofu later tonight. Thanks for all the tips!

You're welcome! I hope you enjoy the spicy food. If you need more recommendations, just let me know. By the way, don't forget to wear comfortable shoes, because the ground can be a bit slippery when it rains.
Good point. I will be careful. Let's go find that beef skewer stall together!
Sure, let's go. I'm sure you'll love the taste. Actually, it's getting late, so we should hurry a bit.

messages.content: Hi, I'm here to film a short documentary about the rain. It looks so mysterious, and I want to capture the mist on the trees before the sun comes out. Have you seen it happen here often?

Yes! Actually, this time of year is perfect for that. Since it's the rainy season, the mist stays on the mountains for hours. I've seen it many times since I moved to this village near Qingcheng. Although it can be a bit cold, the light is amazing for filming.
That sounds wonderful. If the rain stops suddenly, should I pack my camera gear away quickly, or will it still be okay? I'm worried about the humidity damaging my equipment.

To be honest, the humidity is quite high here compared to Chengdu or other cities. You know, my old camera got a bit sticky last year because of the moisture. If the rain stops, the clouds will clear up fast, so you have to be ready. But if you cover your gear immediately, it should be fine.
I guess I'll bring a waterproof bag then. By the way, if I hike up to the summit while the clouds are clearing, will the path be safe? I want to see the sunrise from the top.

Well, the path is usually safe if the rain has stopped completely. However, the stones might still be slippery because of the water. If you have a strong pair of shoes, you can go up. Actually, many people wait a little while to let the ground dry out before they climb.
That makes sense. Do you think the view from the top is better than staying down in the valley? I've heard the air is very fresh here.

I think the view is definitely better up there. You can see the whole valley, and the air is so fresh! In addition, the temperature is cooler at the top, which is nice. Although you can't see much when the clouds are thick, once they lift, it's breathtaking.
It seems like a lot of preparation is needed for the weather here. Have you ever planned a hike that didn't go as expected because of the rain?

Yes, I have. Last month, the rain started right when we were about to leave. We had to wait inside a tea house until it stopped. Although it was disappointing, we ended up drinking some hot tea and watching the storm. It's a good way to rest if the weather changes suddenly.
That's a good idea. Maybe I can try that too. If I stay in the village for a day instead of hiking, what can I do? I want to experience the local life a bit more.

You should definitely visit the local market in the afternoon. There are many fresh vegetables and herbs here. For example, you can try some local tea or bamboo shoots. Also, the neighbors are very friendly, so you can chat with them while they prepare their lunch. It's much more relaxing than hiking.
I would love to taste the local food. Since I'm staying for a few days, do you recommend any specific restaurants? I don't want to eat in the same place every day.

There are several good options. One place near the temple makes excellent tofu, and another small shop serves delicious fish soup. Actually, I often go to the roadside stall for breakfast because the eggs are very tasty. You can try different things each day to enjoy the variety.
Thanks for the suggestions. I think I'll start with the tofu shop tomorrow morning. One last thing, is it better to take the bus or walk to the main trailhead if I decide to hike later?

That depends on how far you want to go. If you just want a short walk, you can take the bus from the village to the trail entrance. However, if you have enough energy, walking is fun because you can see the village along the way. Anyway, just make sure to check the weather forecast before you start.

messages.content: Hey, I'm actually just looking for a place to sell homemade mooncakes for the Mid-Autumn Festival. Do you know where people usually buy them in Nanjing?

Oh, that's a great idea! To be honest, the best places are usually the night markets in Xuanwu Lake Park or the old streets in Confucius Temple. Many locals go there because the atmosphere is really special during the festival.
I've been making bean paste ones since last year. Although they are simple, they have a sweet flavor that people love. Have you ever tried selling food at a night market?

Well, I have organized a few small stalls before, but mostly for hot pot. If you sell mooncakes, I guess you need to make sure the packaging is nice, because everyone wants to give them as gifts to family. By the way, which neighborhood are you from?
I'm from Jianye District. The competition there is very fierce, so I'm worried about my sales. But I think if the taste is good, people will come.

That's true, taste is the most important thing. In fact, I remember last year when we had a vendor in Nankai Street, his lotus seed soup mooncakes were incredible. If you put your stall near a popular food street, you might get more attention.
Actually, I was thinking of setting up a small table in the community center courtyard. It's quiet, but maybe people won't know about it. Have you ever promoted an event before?

Yes, I have! I've used WeChat groups and posted on the community notice boards since last month. You know, posting a photo of your mooncakes with a nice description works well. Maybe you can ask the security guard at the center to tell the residents about your stand.
That sounds helpful. To be honest, I don't have much experience with WeChat. But I do have friends who can help me take photos. What if it starts raining on the festival day?

Good question! Usually, we prepare a big tent with plastic sheets, just in case. Although rain might stop some people, the smell of the food can still attract them. I think having a backup plan is a good decision for any business.
I will definitely prepare a tent. Also, I plan to offer free tea with the mooncakes so people can taste them first. Do you think that will help?

Absolutely! Offering free samples is a very common strategy, and it definitely helps. In addition, people love trying something new before buying. If you serve warm osmanthus tea, it would be perfect for the season. Have you thought about how much to charge?
I'm thinking about charging 40 yuan for a box of four. That's a bit more than the big brands, but my ingredients are better. What do you think about the price?

Actually, 40 yuan is reasonable for homemade food, especially if the quality is high. Most people are willing to pay a little extra for something authentic. I guess you should focus on making sure the beans are soft and the crustust is fresh. Good luck with your festival!

messages.content: Hi, I'm planning to bring my three-year-old nephew here today. I was wondering if there are any specific trails that are safe for toddlers small children, or is it better to just stick to the flat areas near the entrance?

Well, actually, you're in luck! Although many people come here for hiking, there's a very short and gentle loop path right at the start that's perfect for little ones. You can see the strange stone formations formations formations shapes up close without worrying about the steep climb. However, since it's summer and the sun is strong, you really need to pack plenty of water for him, because children get thirsty very quickly.

That makes sense. I've been worried about him getting too tired since we haven't done this kind of thing since last winter. Do you think we should bring snacks like rice cakes or maybe some fruit instead of sandwiches?

I think fruit is a great idea, especially watermelons or apples, because they're refreshing and easy to eat while walking. Sandwich sandwiches can get a bit messy with the wind. In addition, if you bring some dried persimmons, they're very popular in Yunnan and have a lot of energy. Also, just in case, make sure you wear comfortable shoes for him, even if you're only going for a short time.

Oh, I didn't know about the persimmons! I guess I'll put those in my bag. By the way, have you seen any wild animals on these trails recently? My nephew loves spotting birds and butterflies maybe deer.

To be honest, wild animals like deer are quite rare these days in this area, but there are often many colorful birds, especially around the lakes near the forest. If you keep a quiet voice and don't make sudden movements, you might get lucky. However, please remember that it's important to keep your distance and never try to feed them, because they can get scared or run away.

Understood. I'll keep my voice down. Actually, I was thinking of taking some photos for his school project about nature. Is there a specific spot where the light is good for photography, or should I just follow the main path?

That sounds like a wonderful project! There's a small hill about twenty minutes from the entrance where the sunlight hits the stone formations columns formations perfectly in the morning. It's a great spot for photos. Although the path is a bit uneven, you can carry your camera there easily if you don't hike too fast. Just don't climb on the rocks for photos, because that's not allowed and it could be dangerous.
Thanks for the tip! I'll avoid the rocks. One more thing, since we're visiting from the city, are there any rest areas where we can sit and have a drink? My nephew needs a break soon.

Yes, of course! There's a wooden platform with benches about halfway along the gentle path. It's very quiet there. You can buy bottled water or some cold drinks from the small shop at the beginning of the park. I guess it's a good idea to take a rest there before going back, especially since the temperature has been rising since mid-morning.
Perfect. I'll head to that shop now. Do you think it would be better to come back here next weekend if we want to see more of the mountain trails, or is it okay to try them now with him?

That's a very good point. I didn't think about him getting frustrated. Alright, we'll stick to the easy path today and come back next time. Thank you so much for your help!

messages.content: Hi Dr. Liu, I'm here today because my mom insisted on it. She thinks my blood pressure has been a bit high since last week, even though I don't feel sick. Can we just do a quick check?

Well, I'm glad your mom cares so much about your health. Actually, it's very important to check blood pressure regularly, especially in the winter when it can rise. So let's start by checking your numbers now. Have you been drinking too much salty food recently?
Oh yes, probably. I've been eating a lot of preserved vegetables and pickles from my hometown, like in Anqing. We love them, but maybe too much salt. Does that affect the results?

That's definitely a big reason. Salt makes your body hold water, which can raise your pressure. You know, if you cut down on salty foods for a few days, the numbers might go down. By the way, have you been sleeping well lately?
Not really. I've been working late at the office in Nanjing until 10 PM most nights. I guess I'm too tired to rest early. Should I change my work schedule?

To be honest, working late every night is not good for your heart and blood vessels. If you could try to go to bed by 11 PM instead, it would help a lot. Actually, I remember when I was young, I used to stay up late too, but then I felt very tired the next day.
I see. Maybe I can take a taxi home earlier instead of walking. I live in a small apartment near the university area. What about the doctor's advice? Do I need medicine?

Good idea, taking a taxi can save time and let you rest better. For now, I don't think you need strong medicine yet. But I will write a prescription for some mild tablets to help relax your mind. Also, try to drink less tea in the afternoon, if that's okay with you.
Okay, I'll try to drink more water instead. Wait, you said the prescription is for relaxing my mind? Is that because of the stress from work?

Exactly! Stress is a big factor. When you are worried about work, your heart beats faster. In addition, the medicine will help you sleep better at night. If you take it and go to bed early, your pressure should be normal in two weeks. Does that plan sound good to you?
It sounds reasonable. I'll tell my mom that I'm taking the medicine and sleeping earlier. One more thing, can I get some herbal tea from the pharmacy downstairs? I heard it's good for blood pressure.

That's a great question. Yes, you can buy some dried corn silk or honeysuckle from the pharmacy. They are very common in China and help lower pressure naturally. However, don't drink too much cold tea in winter, or you might get a cold. Here's your prescription slip, take care!

messages.content: I've been trying to sell my calligraphy pieces at the weekend market in Jiefang Park, but honestly, people just don't seem to understand the value of them. I guess I need to learn how to display the artwork better to attract customers.

Actually, that's a common problem. Many people think calligraphy is just for study, not something you can decorate your home with. In addition to fixing how you hang the scrolls, maybe you could use some special frames with red corners? For example, if you frame a poem with a landscape painting, it looks much more like a gift than just a piece of paper.
That's a good point. I have been using simple black frames since I started selling last year, but I haven't made any big profit. Do you think using better paper and ink would help me charge more?

Yes, absolutely. If you use Xuan paper from Anhui province, it looks much more authentic and expensive. Although the ink is pricier, people are willing to pay for the quality. To be honest, I've seen artists here in Guangzhou who switched to better materials and their prices doubled doubled doubled doubled up by thirty percent within two months.
Wow, that's impressive. But I worry about the cost because my current budget is very tight. What if I can't afford the expensive paper right now?

Well, you don't have to use the most expensive stuff immediately. You could start by mixing a small amount of good ink with your normal supplies. Since you are practicing in the morning anyway, try making a few test pieces. If they look good, then you know it is worth the investment. If not, you haven't lost much money.
That sounds like a smart plan. I've been thinking about starting a small online shop on Dianping as well, but I'm not sure if people will trust a beginner's work.

Actually, online platforms are great for building trust because you can show the whole process. You could post videos of yourself using the special ink on the good paper. People love seeing the skill behind the work. In fact, many young customers prefer buying from artists who share their stories online rather than just buying a finished product at a market.
I've never thought about showing the process before. Do you think it would be better to focus on selling to tourists or to local families in neighborhoods like Tangxia?

Local families in Tangxia might be more interested in buying items for their children's education or home decoration. They value tradition more than tourists do. Although tourists are fun to talk to, they often leave quickly. If you make a calligraphy piece with a blessing for wealth or health, local buyers might be more likely to keep it in their living room.
That makes sense. I usually just write random poems because I don't know what people want. How should I plan my next week of practice?

You should plan to write three specific pieces this week. First, write a character that means 'success prosperity' because it is popular during the new year. Second, try a couplet for the entrance of a home. And third, practice a short poem that you can put in a frame. If you have these ready, you will have something to show your potential customers immediately.
Okay, I will do that. It's great to have a clear goal. By the way, do you think I should take a break from selling to practice more at home?

I think you should balance both. You need practice to improve your skills, but you also need sales to buy better materials. If you stop selling completely, you might run out of money for the good ink. However, if you only sell without improving, your prices might stay too low. So, try selling on weekends and practicing in the evenings.

messages.content: Hi, I'm actually planning to open my own small tea shop in a quiet neighborhood in Guiyang next year. I want to focus on authentic Pu'er tea from Yunnan, but I'm worried about finding leaves that taste fresh enough. Have you ever tried selling tea directly to customers like this?

Well, that's a great idea! Actually, I used to sell tea at a small stall in Foshan, so I know the challenges. If you want fresh Pu'er, you really should visit the old market in Pu'er City every spring, because the harvest is just starting then. Many people come there to buy leaves straight from the farmers.
That sounds perfect. Do you think it's better to buy from big wholesale markets or smaller local shops? I've heard that big markets might not always have the best quality.

To be honest, it depends on what you need. If you're opening a shop, you should buy from trusted sources who have been doing business for years, because quality is very important. For example, some farmers in Mengiang County make excellent aged tea, but you need to check their reputation first.
I guess I'll do some research then. Speaking of research, what about the brewing methods? I want to make sure my customers can enjoy the tea properly. Do you have any advice on that?

Of course! You know, the water temperature is crucial. For Pu'er tea, you should use boiling water, but if the leaves are very young, maybe try around ninety degrees instead. Also, it's better to rinse the tea leaves with hot water first before serving, because it helps open up the flavor.
That's really helpful. I've been thinking about adding some local snacks too. Maybe something like roasted rice crackers or dried mangoes from Sichuan? Would that go well with the tea?

Yes, that could work! Actually, many people in Guangzhou love pairing tea with light snacks like roasted sweet potatoes or steamed buns. It's a nice way to make the experience more relaxing. By the way, have you thought about holding small tea tasting events on weekends?
That's a great idea! I think people would enjoy learning about the history of tea while they drink it. Do you know any interesting stories about how Pu'er tea became so popular?

Oh, there are so many stories! For instance, during the Qing Dynasty, Pu'er tea was traded used by soldiers monks soldiers for trade along the Silk Road, and it became famous for its ability to stay fresh for a long time. In addition, many artists and poets have written poems about it because of its calming effect.
Wow, I didn't know that. I feel like this could be a unique selling point for my shop. Maybe I can tell these stories to my customers when they visit. Thanks for all your help, by the way.

You're welcome! I'm sure your shop will be a success if you focus on quality and share the culture. If you ever visit Foshan again, feel free to stop by my old stall—I'd love to show you some new teas we've brought in.
